items.title: BlackRock expands AI push with new robotics ETF as investor enthusiasm cools
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: BlackRock has launched a new robotics focused ETF as investors become more selective about AI investments. The fund targets companies using intelligent machines across industries such as manufacturing and transportation, adding to a rapidly expanding market of ETFs built around different parts of the AI theme.
items.body: BlackRock has added another AI focused exchange traded fund to its growing lineup, turning to robotics as investors become more selective about where they place their bets on the technology theme, according to Reuters.The global asset manager launched the iShares Future Robotics and Related Technologies ETF on Wednesday, targeting companies that use intelligent machines to automate repetitive tasks across industries including transportation and manufacturing.Robotics seen as next leg of AI adoptionBlackRock sees robotics as an important part of the next phase of AI adoption, with intelligent machines potentially extending the technology's reach beyond software and data centres into a wider range of industries.The new fund comes as investors' enthusiasm for AI has encountered bouts of volatility. BlackRock US head of equity ETFs Jay Jacobs said the recent swings showed that AI exposure is becoming a more complicated investment theme, Reuters reported.“Recent volatility is a reminder that AI is not a single trade and that investors need to be deliberate about where and how they take exposure, Jacobs said.He added that the volatility had not changed BlackRock's conviction in the broader AI theme.AI ETF market keeps expandingThe new fund also adds to an increasingly crowded market of ETFs built around the AI investment story. Investors already have access to scores of ETFs explicitly tracking AI, alongside technology focused funds with significant exposure to major AI linked companies such as Nvidia and Micron, according to Reuters.At least six AI linked ETFs have launched over the past month, with several targeting specific corners of the industry rather than taking a broad approach.Global X recently introduced the LLM ETF, focused on companies developing large language models, while Defiance launched an ETF targeting bonds issued by AI infrastructure companies, Reuters reported.Jacobs said expectations around AI can change quickly, while adoption may develop unevenly and market risk remains concentrated among a relatively narrow group of companies.“Expectations can shift quickly, adoption can develop unevenly and market risk remains concentrated in a relatively narrow group of companies, he said.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 

３営業日ぶりに反発して取引を終えた。石油株が買われ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反発した。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．３１％高だった。

石油大手のＢＰは１．９％、シェルは０．２％それぞれ上昇。北海のジャックドー・ガス田の採掘を英政府が承認した。

資産運用会社アバディーンは４．１％安。一部で資金流入の回復が予想より遅れるとの見通しを示し、売られた。上半期決算を発表した自転車・自動車部品販売のハルフォーズは８．６％安。

ヒーリー財務相の予算案発表を来週に控える中、公的部門の純借入額は２カ月連続で市場予想を上回った。公的債務残高は３兆ポンド（約４兆１００億ドル）を超えた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞ 

反発して取引を終えた。堅調な業績を示した企業が物色される中、抗議デモ激化に伴う政治不安から下落していたフランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は１．０６％高と買い戻しの動きが出た。

オランダの人材サービス大手ランスタッドは２０．２％高。直近四半期決算が好感された。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州高級品株１０種指数は１．７２％高。フランスの高級眼鏡大手エシロールルックスオティカは１５．５％上昇。

増収決算となったデンマークの物流大手ＤＳＶは１５．１％上昇した。

一方、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種自動車・部品株指数は１．７２％安。フランスの大手タイヤメーカー、ミシュランは７．２％下落した。

フランスの小売大手カルフールは１３．８％安。暴動や略奪、夜間外出禁止令による影響を踏まえて通期業績予想を下方修正し、値下がりした。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　

域内国債利回りが上昇した。フランスで抗議行動が広がり、ぜい弱な財政と政治的不透明感への懸念が一段と強まった。

フランスの指標となる１０年物国債（ＯＡＴ）利回りは、２００２年７月以来初めて５％台に乗せた。この日は８ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）、今週では２０ｂｐ超上昇した。

独仏１０年債利回り格差＜DE１０FR１０=RR＞は１５０ｂｐと、ユーロ圏主要国債市場で最大となった。１０月初めに付けた約１６０ｂｐの１５年ぶり高水準に向けて再び拡大しつつある。

フランスの混乱は２０日までにいくぶん落ち着いたが、２４日にはさらなる抗議行動が予定されており、企業は財務面での打撃を感じ始めている。

投資家はイタリアにも注目している。生活費高騰を巡る抗議行動を受け、メローニ首相は２０日、より厳しい暴動対策を承認した。

ただイタリア国債は今週、フランス債よりも堅調で、１０年利回りの上昇は１２ｂｐにとどまった。

イタリア１０年債利回りは８ｂｐ上昇し４．６０４７％となった。独伊１０年債利回り格差は４ｂｐ拡大して１１６ｂｐとなった。

ドイツの１０年債利回りは３．４ｂｐ上昇の３．４２７４％と、今週はほぼ変わらず。２年債利回りは４ｂｐ上昇し３．０９４０％となった。

items.title: メタに250億ドル支払い命令、米地裁　ＦＢ個人情報問題巡り
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Diana Novak Jones

[２１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Diana Novak Jones

[２１日 ロイター] - 米ニューメキシコ州の地裁は２１日、メタ・プラットフォームズに対し２５０億ドルの支払いを命じた。トランプ氏の２０１６年米大統領選陣営に関与した政治コンサルティング会社がフェイスブック利用者数百万人のデータを本人の同意なく取得したとされる問題を巡る訴訟で、州地裁陪審がメタは利用者を欺いたと認定していた。

ニューメキシコ州のラウル・トレス司法長官は、単独の州が企業を相手に勝ち取った判決として、米国史上最大級だと述べた。

地裁のフランシス・マシュー判事は陪審評決を受けた命令で、この件は「フェイスブックの中核的な事業慣行そのものに関わる問題だ」と指摘した。同判事は州法に基づけば２１９０億ドル超の制裁金が妥当と判断したが、２５０億ドルに減額した。

メタのＣ・Ｊ・マホニー最高法務責任者（ＣＬＯ）は声明で、控訴審で勝訴すると確信していると表明した。

同氏は「今回の判断と司法長官による法執行の進め方は、ニューメキシコ州で事業を営むことを事実上不可能にする」と指摘。「この訴訟は本質的に、人々がオンラインで何を発言できるかについて新たな規則を強制するため、言論に税を課そうとするものだ」と述べた。 

メタはこれまで、数十億ドル規模の制裁金は、適正手続きや過大な罰金からの保護を受ける憲法上の権利を侵害する恐れがあると主張していた。

この件を巡っては、英政治コンサルティング会社ケンブリッジ・アナリティカがサードパーティー製アプリを通じて最大８７００万人分のフェイスブック利用者の個人データを収集していたことが明らかになり、ニューメキシコ州の司法長官が２０２１年にメタを提訴していた。

今回の制裁金は、ケンブリッジ・アナリティカ問題を受けてメタに科されたものとしては最大となる。同社は１９年にも、同じ問題を巡り米連邦取引委員会（ＦＴＣ）から５０億ドルの制裁金を科された。

items.title: Rice rescues Arsenal at Bayern as Real Madrid hit four
items.author: Fernando Kallas
items.creator: Fernando Kallas
items.summary: Declan Rice rescued Arsenal with a late equaliser in an electric 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday, while Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 and Como handed Manchester United a bruising defeat by the same score.
items.body:
Declan Rice rescued Arsenal with a late equaliser in an electric 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday, while Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 and Como handed Manchester United a bruising defeat by the same score.
Arsenal's evening in Germany began ominously when Bukayo Saka limped out of the contest in the 10th minute, clutching his knee after falling while attempting a pass.
Fifteen minutes later, however, Eberechi Eze raced on to Martin Odegaard's long ball and fired an angled shot past Manuel Neuer. Initially flagged offside, the goal was awarded following a VAR review.
Bayern replied in the 35th minute when Harry Kane released Alphonso Davies down the left with a through ball from halfway, the Canadian breaking clear before beating David Raya with a composed right-footed finish.
Kane put the hosts ahead from the penalty spot in the 61st minute after his shot struck Jurrien Timber's raised hand, blasting his 58th Champions League goal into the roof of the net.
But Rice had the final say eight minutes from time, exchanging passes with Viktor Gyokeres inside the box before slotting past Neuer.
COURTOIS KEEPS REAL AFLOAT At the Santiago Bernabeu, Real's emphatic scoreline owed much to goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who denied Romulo's close-range volley and thwarted Christopher Nkunku one-on-one before the hosts found their rhythm.
Bernardo Silva broke the deadlock in the 43rd minute, pouncing to tap home almost on the goalline after Leipzig goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt spilled Federico Valverde's shot.
Arda Guler doubled the lead seven minutes after halftime, beating a defender to Kylian Mbappe's goalbound header from Jude Bellingham's cross.
Mbappe curled a shot into the top corner in the 83rd minute before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back a minute later. Substitute Yan Diomande capped Real's victory with a spectacular volley from Brahim Diaz's cross.
Elsewhere, Galatasaray won 4-2 at Lille, Inter Milan edged Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, Aston Villa beat Viking Stavanger 3-1 and Real Betis beat Feyenoord 1-0, while LASK stunned Sporting 3-2 in Lisbon.
Paris St Germain, Aston Villa, Real Madrid, Liverpool and Real Betis top the standings having all made perfect starts to their Champions League campaigns, with three wins from three matches.
Inter Milan overcame Alessandro Bastoni's dismissal to beat Shakhtar Donetsk, Carlos Augusto controlling Henrikh Mkhitaryan's long pass in his stride before scoring the 77th-minute winner.
Bastoni had received a second booking eight minutes earlier for pushing an opponent away from the ball.
Aston Villa comfortably beat Norway's Viking, Ross Barkley heading the opener from a corner before Emiliano Buendia converted a penalty and Alysson found the net with a deflected shot. Peter Christiansen struck Viking's late consolation.
Isco's 59th-minute penalty following a handball gave Real Betis victory over Feyenoord in Seville, while Club Brugge beat Lens 3-0 through goals from Hans Vanaken, Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs.
LASK stunned Sporting, recovering from Luis Suarez's early penalty with goals from Christoph Lang, Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek. Suarez scored again in the 89th minute but the hosts could not salvage a point.
PAZ PUNISHES UNITED Earlier, Nico Paz tormented Manchester United with two goals and an assist as Como swept to victory in northern Italy, while Galatasaray won a six-goal thriller at Lille.
Paz put Como ahead inside two minutes with a curling effort from the edge of the box, then helped double the lead four minutes after halftime, threading a perfectly weighted pass through for Anastasios Douvikas to finish first time past the advancing goalkeeper.
The Argentine then robbed Carlos Baleba near the right touchline and surged diagonally for more than 30 metres before steering a left-footed finish inside the far post.
Jacobo Ramon headed Como's fourth from substitute Kaiki Bruno's cross in the 76th minute, with Joshua Zirkzee grabbing United's stoppage-time consolation from Amad Diallo's delivery.
In France, Galatasaray recovered from surrendering an early lead to beat Lille 4-2.
Yunus Akgun fired the visitors ahead shortly after kickoff, but Soriba Diaoune equalised five minutes later and struck again in the 39th minute to put Lille in front.
Alexey Batrakov headed Galatasaray level in the 44th minute before Lucas Torreira appeared to glance home a corner in the 52nd, although the effort was later credited as a Nabil Bentaleb own goal.
Victor Osimhen completed the scoring nine minutes later with a powerful strike from the edge of the box.

items.title: US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
items.author: Rami Ayyub, Humeyra Pamuk, Timour Azhari
items.creator: Rami Ayyub, Humeyra Pamuk, Timour Azhari
items.summary: The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.
items.body:
The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.
The order came as attacks in Saudi Arabia killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam and two people were killed in a [USN:L1N46710X TEXT:"drone attack on an oil field"].
State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a post on X that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only" amid [USN:L1N4610L5 TEXT:"attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis"] in Yemen on civilian targets in the country.
Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months after many were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities after the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.
"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott said.
Four US officials told Reuters that US missions in other Gulf states would also be ordering family members to leave. Pigott did not address changes to other missions outside Saudi Arabia.
The latest withdrawals follow an escalation of the fighting in Yemen, opening another front in the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The wider conflict has snarled global energy trade and hurt Gulf economies.
After the departure order, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority reported an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight others. Earlier in the day, two people were killed after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, the energy ministry said.
The US embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on Wednesday about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia, after recent deadly strikes including [USN:S8N43T03L TEXT:"on Riyadh's airport"].
The embassy and a CIA station hosted there [USN:L1N3ZR1EN TEXT:"came under attack"] by drones in early March, as Iran began launching attacks across the region.

items.title: ゼレンスキー氏、米ロとの3者協議再開支持　11月上旬までの開催希望
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２１日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[２１日　ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２１日、ロシア、米国、ウクライナの実務レベル協議を早期に開催するとの米国の提案を支持すると表明した。

ゼレンスキー大統領は記者団に対し、協議は遅くとも１１月上旬までの実施が望ましいとし、和平案のほか、首脳レベルの会談の可能性について取り上げられるとの見方を示した。

米国のウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使はゼレンスキー氏と２０日にノルウェーの首都オスロで会談した後、２１日にロシアのプーチン大統領とロシア第２の都市サンクトペテルブルクで会談。ウィットコフ氏との会談を受け、プーチン大統領はウクライナ和平に向けた米国仲介の協議の再開に合意した。

ゼレンスキー氏はノルウェーから首都キーウへの帰途、記者団に対し、ウィットコフ氏がプーチン大統領と会談した後、米政府当局者と協議したと明らかにし、「ロシアが実務レベルの３者協議を支持しているとの説明を受けた。米国は可能な限り早期の開催を提案しており、ウクライナも支持している。ウクライナは米国と連絡を取り合っており、米国は協議を１１月中、できれば１１月上旬までに実施できるよう全力を尽くすと考えている」と語った。

その上で、ウクライナは「停戦、戦争終結、エネルギー施設を対象とした停戦、人道的取り組みなど、いかなる提案も支持する」と述べた。

ロシア大統領府によると、３者協議の開催地としてアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のアブダビが検討されており、１１月１０日、もしくはそれ以降に実施される可能性がある。

Oct 21 : Electronic Arts is planning to close BioWare, the developer of the "Mass Effect" series of games, and lay off employees to focus on more lucrative projects, the company said on Wednesday in an email to employees.
Here are some details:
• EA said it would cancel an early-stage "Mass Effect" project and close BioWare's studio in Edmonton, Canada, marking the end of the developer known for role-playing game franchises such as "Dragon Age"
• EA is planning to cut around 400 jobs, about 3 per cent of its total staff, including roughly 50 at BioWare, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing a person familiar with the company’s plans

• The videogame publisher said it would concentrate on fewer large-scale action-adventure games, while continuing development of "Marvel's Iron Man" and the next "Star Wars Jedi" game
• EA also said it was restructuring the team behind skateboarding simulation "skate." into a smaller, more focused studio
• The company said it would help affected employees explore other opportunities within EA
• EA was taken private in a $55 billion deal led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, which closed in August

items.title: New Mexico sues to stop payouts to Jeffrey Epstein's lawyer, accountant
items.author: Andrew Hay
items.creator: Andrew Hay
items.summary: New Mexico has filed a civil lawsuit to block payments from Jeffrey Epstein's estate to the late sex offender's lawyer and accountant, and to recover damages for survivors of his alleged sexual abuse, the state's top law enforcement official said on Wednesday.
items.body:
New Mexico has filed a civil lawsuit to block payments from Jeffrey Epstein's estate to the late sex offender's lawyer and accountant, and to recover damages for survivors of his alleged sexual abuse, the state's top law enforcement official said on Wednesday.
The suit is the first law enforcement action against Epstein's longtime personal attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn, according to New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez.
The lawsuit alleges Indyke and Kahn facilitated, financed, and concealed Epstein's sex trafficking operation, including at his ranch 30 miles south of New Mexico's capital Santa Fe. They are co-executors of Epstein's estate, valued at $107 million, and respectively eligible for bequests of $50 million and $25 million from it, according to the complaint.
Daniel Weiner, a lawyer representing Indyke and Kahn, rejected allegations the two "knowingly" facilitated Epstein's abuse of women, saying the crimes took place "behind closed doors, in secluded locations" when neither was present.
The suit will test whether authorities are able to pin down allegations that a network of people and financial arrangements helped sustain and conceal Epstein's operations.
“Jeffrey Epstein did not operate alone, and his death does not end the pursuit of accountability for the people who helped make his crimes possible,” Torrez said at a press conference in Albuquerque. He was joined by two survivors of Epstein's alleged abuse, Julia Molchanova and Anouska De Georgiou.
Indyke and Kahn have already been named in civil lawsuits against the Epstein estate, including a complaint last month seeking damages for people pictured in the late financier's [USN:L6N45814E TEXT:"collection"] of child sexual abuse material.
"Not a single woman has ever accused Mr. Indyke or Mr. Kahn of committing sexual abuse or witnessing sexual abuse," Weiner said in a statement, adding that the New Mexico attorney general's office had made no effort to interview the men before filing the lawsuit.
New Mexico's civil action comes after the Democratic-run state in February [USN:L6N3ZF16Q TEXT:"reopened"] an investigation into activities at Epstein's Zorro Ranch in New Mexico, where he is accused of abusing women and girls for nearly three decades.
Eight months into the probe, New Mexico has yet to file any criminal charges.
The state has [USN:L6N442109 TEXT:"sued"] the US Department of Justice for access to unredacted files on Epstein, accusing the Trump administration of stonewalling its investigation.
The DOJ said it provided some files but was [USN:L6N43H116 TEXT:"prevented"] from handing over most material due to privacy protections.
Molchanova and De Georgiou, both prominent survivors of Epstein's sex trafficking network, applauded the New Mexico lawsuit to stop Indyke and Kahn profiting any further from the late sex-offender's estate.
"Accountability cannot end with Epstein and Maxwell, it must extend to those who knowingly made their abuse possible, especially those who stand to profit from it," said De Georgiou, a key witness at the trial of Epstein's partner Ghislaine Maxwell, convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison in 2022 for sex trafficking of a minor and related conspiracy.

items.body: A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta Platforms to pay $25 billion after a jury found that the company misled consumers about its data privacy practices, in a case stemming from allegations that millions of Facebook users' personal information was obtained without their consent, Reuters reported.Judge Francis Mathew ruled on Wednesday that a penalty exceeding $219 billion was warranted under state law but reduced the amount to $25 billion."Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order following the verdict.The lawsuit was filed by New Mexico's attorney general in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party application.The case centres on allegations that Meta misrepresented how it handled users' personal information and addressed harmful content on its platforms.Jury finds more than 43 million violationsNew Mexico accused Meta of misleading Facebook users about who could access their personal data, how the company dealt with hate speech and misinformation, and other internal policies.The state alleged that Meta knew third parties had extensive access to users' information and tolerated harmful content when doing so benefited its business.On September 25, jurors found that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta and its leadership on these issues were misleading. They determined that the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico's consumer protection laws, based on the number of Facebook users or state residents exposed to each misleading statement.State law permits penalties of up to $5,000 per violation. New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said after the verdict that the money would go to the state's school system.State sought up to $40 billion in penaltiesAt an October 1 hearing, Randi McGinn, a lawyer representing New Mexico, asked Judge Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion.McGinn argued that the amount would be consistent with the jury's verdict and the due process protections provided by the US Constitution.Meta, however, urged the court to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion, warning that a significantly higher amount could discourage businesses from operating in the state.In court filings, the company argued that it did not sell users' personal data and that the state had failed to demonstrate that any consumer had actually been misled.The $25 billion order represents a substantial penalty, although it is below the amount sought by the state's legal team and far lower than the figure the judge said was justified under state law.Second major legal setback for Meta in New MexicoThe verdict marks the second time in six months that a Santa Fe jury has ruled against Meta in a lawsuit brought by New Mexico.In the first trial, which concluded in March, jurors found that Meta had misled users about the safety of young people on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. The jury ordered the company to pay $375 million in civil penalties.Following a second phase of that trial, a judge directed Meta to pay an additional $567 million into a New Mexico fund for teen mental health.The court also ordered the company to implement measures to protect teenage users of Facebook and Instagram in the state.The latest ruling adds to Meta's legal challenges over consumer protection, data privacy and online safety, as regulators and governments continue to scrutinise how major technology platforms handle users' information and address harmful content.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２１日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[２１日　ロイター] - エジプトのシシ大統領は、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派がサウジアラビアに対する攻撃を激化させる中、サウジに対するエジプトの軍事支援はサウジの領土と国境の防衛に限定され、イエメンへの攻撃は含まれないと述べた。大統領府が２１日、明らかにした。

サウジ国営通信ＳＰＡによると、シシ氏の発言は、エジプトのアブデルアティ外相とラシャド国家情報局（ＧＩＳ）長官がリヤドで行った、サウジのムハンマド・ビン・サルマン皇太子との会談に合わせて出された。 

ＳＰＡによると、アブデルアティ外相はシシ氏からの書簡をサルマン国王に手渡し、両国関係や地域の情勢について協議した。

シシ氏はまた、要請があれば他のアラブ諸国の領土も防衛するとした一方、エジプトの軍事行動はエジプト領内、またはエジプトが安全・安定の保護を目指すアラブ諸国の領内を越えて及ぶことはないと述べた。

エジプトによるサウジへの軍事支援は、中東紛争の大幅な拡大を意味する可能性がある。今年２月に米国とイスラエルがイランを攻撃して以来、世界のエネルギー供給は混乱し、原油価格を押し上げている。

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 21 : BlackRock rolled out another in a suite of exchange-traded funds tied to AI on Wednesday, even as the willingness of investors to wholeheartedly embrace the theme has hit speed bumps.
The global asset manager said that its iShares Future Robotics and Related Technologies ETF will invest in companies that use intelligent machines to streamline repetitive tasks in industries such as transportation and manufacturing, which it said represents the next frontier in AI technologies.
“Recent volatility is a reminder that AI is not a single trade and that investors need to be deliberate about where and how they take exposure," said Jay Jacobs, US head of equity ETFs at BlackRock. That volatility does not change the firm's conviction on the AI theme, he added.
"Expectations can shift quickly, adoption can develop unevenly and market risk remains concentrated in a relatively narrow group of companies," Jacobs said. Moreover, AI has emerged as a driver of both returns and risk even in broad market portfolios.

Investors can choose from scores of ETFs that explicitly track the AI investment thesis, and dozens more technology-focused funds that have a heavy exposure via outsize stakes in stocks such as Micron or Nvidia.
At least six AI-linked ETFs have made their debut in the past month, many focusing on more narrow AI-related themes rather than offering broad AI products. For instance, Global X recently introduced the LLM ETF, which offers exposure to companies developing new large language models, while Defiance has launched the first ETF to target the bonds of AI infrastructure companies.
BlackRock said it believes robotics is key to the next wave of AI adoption in a variety of sectors.

items.title: Chevron to sharpen US Gulf focus with sale of older assets
items.author: David French, Sheila Dang
items.creator: David French, Sheila Dang
items.summary: Chevron is exploring the sale of some of its older oil and gas assets in the US Gulf, the company confirmed to Reuters, part of an effort to focus on high-growth developments in the region.
items.body:
Chevron (CVX.N) is exploring the sale of some of its older oil and gas assets in the US Gulf, the company confirmed to Reuters, part of an effort to focus on high-growth developments in the region.
The energy producer is in the early stages of a multi-month process that could see a number of assets offloaded, a Chevron spokesperson said in response to questions from Reuters about the sale effort.
"We are initiating the process of marketing some of our mature Gulf of America producing assets, including Petronius, Tubular Bells, and Llano as well as working interest in several other operated and non-operated fields," the spokesperson said.
The move is part of Chevron's efforts to ensure its portfolio aligns with the company's priorities, the spokesperson said, adding there was no guarantee that sales would take place.
With Chevron targeting production from the US Gulf to grow to 300,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by the end of this year, the portfolio-trimming efforts indicate Chevron is increasingly focused on newer projects and opportunities in the region.
This would include [USN:L1N3JZ01X TEXT:"Anchor"], its first platform producing at ultra-high subsea pressure, and Ballymore, which began production last year. The company is also pursuing exploration to find oil and gas resources near existing facilities, and has been a [USN:L1N3ZZ0X3 TEXT:"top spender"] in recent sales of drilling rights in the US Gulf conducted by the Interior Department.
SHARPENING FOCUS Market conditions are favorable for Chevron's pruning efforts. There continues to be heightened buyer interest in American energy production, and asset valuations are supported by elevated oil prices -- US crude touched a six-month high on Tuesday.
The sales will likely raise around $1 billion for the company, said two people aware of the sale effort, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential deliberations.
Buyer interest is expected to come from international operators that specialize in offshore development and that are seeking to grow their US Gulf footprint, as well as US companies focused on the basin. Other energy majors may also show interest, the sources added.
Petronius began producing in 2000, and Tubular Bells in 2014, according to Chevron's website. The company owns 100% of Tubular Bells, having initially held 43% but assumed the rest following its takeover of Hess. Chevron operates Petronius with Talos Energy (TALO.N) as its partner in the platform.
Chevron's 50% position in Llano was also inherited from Hess. Production from the play, which is operated by Shell (SHEL.L) , started in 2004.

items.title: China’s Chery Picks Omoda C4 as Its First Vehicle to Be Built in South Africa
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Nqobile Dludla Chinese automaker Chery Group will begin vehicle production in South Africa with its Omoda C4 crossover SUV, deepening its presence in Africa. The Omoda C4 will be produced at the Rosslyn plant near Pretoria, which Chery acquired from Nissan this year. It …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
By Nqobile Dludla

Chinese automaker Chery Group will begin vehicle production in South Africa with its Omoda C4 crossover SUV, deepening its presence in Africa.

The Omoda C4 will be produced at the Rosslyn plant near Pretoria, which Chery acquired from Nissan this year. It will be offered in gasoline, hybrid and fully electric variants when it launches for sale in South Africa next year, the company said on Wednesday.

Chery said production would be accompanied by a localization program aimed at developing South African suppliers and increasing the proportion of locally sourced components. That chimes with South African initiatives to increase domestic manufacturing and component sourcing.

Chinese automakers including BYD, Chery and Great Wall Motor (GWM) are accelerating their push into overseas markets, including Africa, as slowing growth at home and intense competition in China’s crowded auto sector force manufacturers to seek new buyers abroad.

Beijing Automotive Group (BAIC) has an assembly and manufacturing plant in South Africa while GWM is considering whether to share a manufacturing facility with another carmaker or acquire an existing plant if available.

South Africa, now the continent’s second-biggest automotive manufacturing hub, has become a key target for Chinese brands looking to build market share.

Chery has said it wants to establish South Africa as its African hub for manufacturing, exports, research and development.

The Omoda C4, aimed at younger buyers, will join a growing lineup of models set for local production at the plant, including the Jetour T series of SUVs.

During the ramp-up phase in the third and fourth quarters of 2027, the company expects to produce 15,000 vehicles, rising eventually to 50,000 a year.

items.body:
Buyout firm CVC (CVC.AS) is exploring a bid to take Swedish security firm Verisure (VSURE.ST) private, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, less than a year after private equity firm Hellman & Friedman floated the company in Stockholm.
Here are some details:
Verisure, which provides professionally monitored security services across 18 countries in Europe and Latin America, was listed in October 2025 at a valuation of 13.7 billion euros ($15.39 billion)
The company's market value has since fallen to about 9.7 billion euros, according to LSEG data, with its shares down more than 33% so far this year
Reuters could not immediately verify the report, while Verisure and CVC declined to comment
CVC's interest is at an early stage and there is no certainty a deal will materialise, the report said
Hellman & Friedman remains Verisure's largest shareholder with a 43.62% stake, LSEG data show
($1 = 0.8898 euros)

items.title: US Treasury yields slip as AI concerns boost safe haven demand ahead of 20 year auction
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: US Treasury yields slipped as investors weighed the impact of higher borrowing costs on AI stocks, with the 10 year yield heading for a second straight daily decline. The move came ahead of a $13 billion 20 year Treasury auction, while markets continued to price in a muted chance of a Fed rate hike.
items.body: US Treasury yields slipped on Wednesday as investors weighed the impact of higher borrowing costs on AI related stocks, while the market awaited a $13 billion auction of 20 year bonds later in the day, according to a Reuters report.The move came as recent swings in AI stocks continued to influence the bond market. Concerns over the heavy spending needed to build AI infrastructure have raised questions about how higher interest rates could affect companies such as CoreWeave. When those concerns weigh on equities, investors have at times shifted towards Treasuries, pushing yields lower.The benchmark 10 year Treasury yield fell 1.5 basis points to 5.102%, putting it on track for a second consecutive daily decline. The 30 year yield slipped 1.2 basis points to 5.413%, while the 2 year yield declined 0.9 basis point to 4.778%.AI volatility keeps bond investors alertUS stocks were slightly higher on Wednesday, helped by a surge in SpaceX shares after its quarterly results eased some concerns around the AI sector. CoreWeave shares, however, fell, highlighting the uneven reaction among AI linked stocks. There has been a very clear trade off across capital markets in almost a risk on, risk off rotation where equities will draw down and we'll see flows in and out of the Treasury market, said Bill Northey, senior investment director at U.S. Bank Wealth Management, Billings, Montana, according to Reuters.Northey said the 10 year Treasury yield at 5.1% was also becoming competitive with equities for investors seeking returns in fixed income.Fed hike bets remain subduedThe bond market's move lower in yields came despite hotter than expected inflation readings. Markets are pricing in a 14.9% chance of a 25 basis point Fed rate hike at the October 28 policy meeting, down from 33.2% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Treasury supply is also in focus, with the US government set to auction $13 billion of 20 year bonds on Wednesday and $26 billion of five year TIPS on Thursday.The 10 year yield has already fallen 14.6 basis points this week, its biggest weekly decline in eight months, after AI related concerns triggered a broader equity selloff and drove investors towards safer assets, according to Reuters.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, wife donate $75 million to Vanderbilt University for new design college
items.author: Livemint
items.summary: The new institution will be named the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design. The campus is expected to open in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, and will build on the legacy of the California College of the Arts
items.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, have donated $75 million to Vanderbilt University to establish a new college focused on art, architecture and design at its planned San Francisco campus.
Announced on July 21, 2026, the contribution is intended to bring creative disciplines together with technology, engineering and entrepreneurship. According to the university, the donation has helped attract additional philanthropic commitments, taking total support for the San Francisco campus beyond $100 million.
The new institution will be named the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design. The campus is expected to open in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, and will build on the legacy of the California College of the Arts (CCA).
Matching gift attracts additional contributionsThe Huang family's donation is structured as a matching gift designed to encourage other donors to support Vanderbilt's expansion in San Francisco.The university said alumni and other supporters had made additional commitments following the announcement. Early contributors include Katie and Matt Paige, Jeff and Marieke Rothschild, and Leah and Ben Spero. The fundraising effort has also received commitments from anonymous donors and members of the Bay Area's arts and creative communities.Vanderbilt said it had secured more than 40% of the funding required to fulfil the full matching commitment by December 31, 2028. The funds will support the establishment and operation of the new college, alongside other academic programmes planned for the campus.College to combine creative and technical educationThe proposed college will integrate studio practice and design laboratories with technical education, engineering and entrepreneurship. Vanderbilt plans to offer undergraduate and graduate degrees, as well as community arts programmes, pre-collegiate courses and lifelong-learning opportunities.The programmes will be subject to the necessary academic reviews and regulatory approvals.Explaining the rationale behind the contribution, Huang said in Vanderbilt's announcement: “Technology expands what we can build. Art and design determine why we build it. Together they shape civilization.”The initiative reflects the couple's stated belief that artistic creativity and design can contribute to technological progress, business innovation and the cultural development of cities.Vanderbilt expects the San Francisco campus to accommodate approximately 1,000 undergraduate and graduate students, alongside full-time faculty and staff. The project forms part of the university's broader expansion beyond its main campus in Nashville, Tennessee.Vanderbilt plans to preserve California College of the Arts legacyThe San Francisco project will build on CCA's nearly 120-year history. Vanderbilt and CCA have agreed that CCA will contribute its campus to Vanderbilt after its operations wind down, subject to customary regulatory and other transaction requirements.Vanderbilt also plans to establish the California College of the Arts Institute to preserve and extend the institution's artistic and cultural legacy.The proposed institute will include the Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts, preserve and digitise CCA's archives, and support artists, designers, architects, curators and scholars through fellowships and residencies.The university has begun a national search for the founding dean of the new college. Its opening remains contingent on the required approvals, with the first students expected in 2027.Separate initiative supports AI and scientific research
The Vanderbilt donation is separate from another philanthropic initiative involving the Huang family.
In May 2026, Reuters reported that the foundation run by Jensen and Lori Huang had purchased computing time from CoreWeave and donated it to universities and nonprofit organisations for scientific and artificial intelligence research. A regulatory filing valued the donated computing resources at $108.3 million. Nvidia also planned to provide free engineering services to some recipients.
CoreWeave uses Nvidia-designed graphics processing units for AI workloads. Reuters noted that Nvidia had invested $2 billion in CoreWeave and agreed to purchase $6.3 billion in cloud capacity from the company, relationships that had raised investor concerns about potential circular financing.
While the computing initiative focuses on research infrastructure, the Vanderbilt contribution is aimed at creating an academic institution that connects art, design and technology.

items.title: Ontario housing market set for modest rebound in 2027: Desjardins report
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: A new report says Ontario’s housing market is expected to improve “modestly” next year as favourable economic conditions help push buyers off the sidelines.
items.body: TORONTO — A new report says Ontario’s housing market is expected to improve “modestly” next year as favourable economic conditions help push buyers off the sidelines, though higher borrowing costs could dull the extent of the rebound. Desjardins senior economist Kari Norman said the province’s housing sector “is in the midst of a striking contradiction.” Her report called the market “weak” despite improved affordability, greater buyer choice and easing rental conditions. The forecast predicts existing home sales will rise nearly five per cent in 2027 compared with this year, driven by lower prices, rising disposable incomes, policy supports for first‑time buyers and some release of pent‑up demand. But activity would still be well below long‑term norms, the report noted, while balanced market conditions should lead to average price growth of 2.4 per cent next year. The analysis said the interest rate backdrop will “likely remaining challenging.” “Home prices are down and at the same time, over the last several years, household income has risen,” Norman said in an interview. “On the other hand, interest rates went up steeply coming out of the pandemic and they have come down, but not to the levels that we saw ... early in the pandemic when interest rates were rock-bottom levels.” Norman said she expects two near-term rate hikes by the Bank of Canada, including later this month when the central bank is set to release its next rate decision. The bank’s key policy rate has been set at 2.25 per cent since October 2025. Rate hikes could limit affordability gains from recent home price declines and rising disposable incomes, Norman said. “That feeds directly into variable rate mortgages,” she said. “Bond rates have already started to rise and that has had an impact on fixed mortgage rates and also on the cost to developers who need, of course, to borrow money in order to have the financing to break ground on projects.” The report projected housing starts in Ontario to rise around six per cent to nearly 65,000 units in 2027 — still more than 30 per cent below levels seen in 2021 and 2022. The primary driver will be rental construction, while condominium starts are also expected to edge higher. The report said ground‑oriented housing starts should ease modestly in 2027, remaining historically weak. With new condo and purpose‑built rental completions adding supply at a time when population growth is likely to be weak, the report said rental conditions should remain relatively balanced. It projects average rents to increase around 1.4 per cent as long‑term tenants could face hikes despite asking rents declining. Norman highlighted two main factors carrying over from 2026 that could threaten her outlook for next year. She said risks to her forecast include lingering trade tensions between Canada and the United States, along with inflationary pressures tied to higher global oil prices due to war in the Middle East. Both factors could drive costs higher across various sectors, raising inflation even further and prompting increased borrowing costs. “And as interest rates go up, it becomes more expensive for both developers to finance new construction and for prospective homebuyers to buy homes,” she said. --- Sammy Hudes, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 21, 2026.

items.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty to New Mexico in data privacy case
items.author: Diana Jones
items.creator: Diana Jones
items.summary: The ruling came in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent.
items.body:
A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms (META.O) on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after [USN:L6N45F10O TEXT:"a jury found"] the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history.
The ruling came in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data.
"Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict.
Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25 billion.
In a statement, C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal.
“This ruling, and the Attorney General's approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico," Mahoney said. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online."
New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said in a statement after the ruling the penalty was one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history.
Meta previously faced [USN:KCN1UJ1L9 TEXT:"a $5 billion penalty"] from the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Six other states settled their lawsuits against Meta related to Cambridge Analytica for $459.2 million as part of a [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"$17.1 billion multistate settlement"] the company reached in August to resolve states' claims that the company's platforms had harmed teen mental health.
LAWSUIT FILED FIVE YEARS AGO New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had [USN:L1N33D09I TEXT:"harvested personal data"] from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.
The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech and misinformation posted on the platform. It alleged the company knew third parties had broad access to users' data and tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company's bottom line.
Cambridge Analytica, now defunct, used the data for voter profiling and targeting.
"It has been a long time coming holding Big Tech accountable," Torrez told a press conference in Albuquerque after Wednesday's ruling. "I think today's judgment is a clear break with that past and a very clear warning to those in this space and beyond that we intend to protect our people and protect our consumers."
Mathew's decision comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits and pressure from lawmakers over the impact of Instagram and Facebook on teen mental health, with another trial slated to begin next week.
Earlier this year, New Mexico won $942 million in a [USN:L6N4431IA TEXT:"pair of"] [USN:L6N40B0XV TEXT:"trials"] against Meta over claims it facilitated sexual exploitation of young people on Instagram and Facebook and misled consumers about the platforms' safety.
Analyst Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson & Co, called the latest New Mexico ruling costly but unlikely to impact the company's value.
"Meta is worth nearly two trillion dollars, and will likely continue to appeal these cases and drag them out," Luria said.
EXPERTS EXPECT LONG APPEAL FIGHT Jurors in September had found that the company and its leadership made 26 misleading statements on data privacy, hate speech and other subjects. Multiplying those statements by their potential audience, they said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws.
At a hearing on October 1, Randi McGinn, a lawyer for New Mexico, had asked Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion.
"This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the value of its stock price," McGinn said.
In court filings, Meta urged Mathew to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion. The evidence showed that Meta does not sell user data and New Mexico did not prove that any consumer had actually been misled, the company said in court filings.

items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Courtney Rozen

[ワシントン ２１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Courtney Rozen

[ワシントン ２１日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業オープンＡＩのブロックマン社長が、ＡＩ規制強化に反対する政治団体「リーディング・ザ・フューチャー」に対し、夫婦で計２５００万ドルを寄付したことが取り沙汰されている。オープンＡＩを巡っては、開発中のＡＩエージェントがシステムに不正侵入する問題が発生。経営陣は連邦政府による規制を訴えている中での多額の寄付の存在が明らかになり、米政府による規制導入を望んでいるのかどうか真意をいぶかる声が出ている。

団体は米国での「ＡＩ開発を過度に制約あるいは遅らせる」規制に反対を掲げ、１１月の米中間選挙に向けて、連邦議会上下両院の少なくとも４８の選挙区に絡んで数百万ドルを投じている。広報担当は「強力かつ責任ある国レベルの規制枠組みを推進するため、議会で協力できる支持者」を求めていると表明したが、寄付に関しては言及しなかった。

オープンＡＩはブログで、ブロックマン夫妻の寄付は個人的なものだと説明している。

トランプ米大統領は今年９月、オープンＡＩほかＡＩ開発主要６社とＡＩの脅威に自主的に対処するとの合意を発表した。規制強化をすれば、新モデルの発表遅延や安全面の懸念による性能変更などにつながり、業界の利益を損なう可能性がある。アンソロピックは、連邦規制が州法に優先することに反対する政治団体に、少なくとも４０００万ドルを寄付している。

items.title: Tesla cuts spending before potential SpaceX deal even as Musk bets future on AI, robots
items.summary: Tesla cut its annual capital expenditure forecast by a fifth and posted surprise positive free cash flow in the third quarter on Wednesday, after investing far less in its AI and robotics ambitions ...
items.body:
Tesla cuts spending before potential SpaceX deal even as Musk bets future on AI, robots
Reuters | Updated: 22-10-2026 05:26 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 05:26 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Tesla cut its annual capital expenditure forecast by a fifth and posted surprise positive free cash flow in the third quarter on Wednesday, after investing far less in its AI and robotics ambitions than Wall Street had expected. The unexpected cash generated in the quarter comes at a critical moment for Tesla, as CEO Elon Musk explores combining the EV maker with his far more capital-intensive space venture, SpaceX.
While the lower spending strengthens Tesla’s financial position ahead of any deal, preserving cash at the expense of investment — in AI, robotaxis and humanoid robots — could undermine the very growth story investors are betting on. Tesla shares, which had risen 2% in after-hours trading after the company reported positive cash flow, higher gross margin and market-beating revenue, reversed course to trade down 2%. They have fallen about 14% this year.
"The free cash flow beat was a pleasant surprise, but when combined with the lower-than-expected capex, raises questions on the next step for the automaker," said Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, which offers ETFs tied to Tesla. "Lower capex suggests less of an 'all-in' approach to the AI arms race than one would expect from Elon." Tesla said it expected capital expenses for 2026 to be roughly $20 billion, down from its previous forecast of more than $25 billion, but did not say what it would spend less on.
In the third quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion in capex, double that of a year ago, but lower than the $7.5 billion analysts on average were expecting, according to LSEG data. Tesla reported free cash flow of $1.53 billion, compared with an expected $4.92 billion cash burn. SPACEX MERGER UNDER DISCUSSION
Musk said on Tuesday that a merger between Tesla and SpaceX was a "good idea" and that the companies had formed special committees to discuss a deal. On Wednesday, Musk said on a conference call with analysts that he had no more to say on the matter. A merger would create a single company at the center of Musk's long-term vision: an integrated technology and manufacturing empire spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.
Still, investors will seek evidence that Tesla is investing enough to turn Musk’s ambitions into commercial businesses, with the robotaxi rollout lagging his promises. Tesla's energy unit has recently offered a counterweight to its auto business, which remains under scrutiny as rivals globally launch newer, often cheaper models. Tesla still leans heavily on the aging Model 3 and Model Y. "The merger still faces a high bar, but tonight’s numbers make the financial logic harder to ignore," said Thomas Monteiro, a senior analyst at Investing.com.
"The main takeaway is that Tesla's surprisingly positive cash flow quarter did not come from stronger profits, but from spending billions less than planned at a time when SpaceX is preparing to invest up to $40 billion in a single quarter." REVENUE FLAT BUT BEATS ESTIMATES
Revenue was flat from a year earlier, despite the end of US tax credits that supported sales last year. That was enough to top Wall Street targets. Net income plunged 43%. Tesla said in a statement that it ended the quarter with the largest backlog for its passenger vehicles in four years. High gasoline prices have stoked demand for EVs, especially in Europe.
With 486,532 vehicles delivered in the third quarter, Tesla is on track to increase annual deliveries for the first time in three years. "Demand is growing rapidly for our vehicles. It's exceeding our production by a significant margin," Musk said on the conference call with analysts. "In a nutshell, after many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth."
The FSD (supervised) attach rate reached over three-quarters of new vehicle deliveries in North America, a nearly 20-percentage-point increase from the second quarter, Tesla said. Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, came in at 18.1% in the third quarter, higher than analysts’ estimates of 16.7%, according to Visible Alpha data.
Tesla said it was aiming to produce 5 million vehicles a year by about 2030, up from an expected 2.5 million this year.

Reuters US Domestic News Summary
Reuters | Updated: 22-10-2026 05:23 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 05:23 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Following is a summary of current US domestic news briefs.
US congressional candidate Brad Lander released after being detained by Israeli military in West Bank
Brad Lander, a US Democratic Party candidate for Congress, was detained by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, along with other Americans and Israelis harvesting olives alongside Palestinian farmers, rights groups said. Lander wrote on X that he had been released with a warning, which he said was apparently due to his public profile, but said several dozen rabbis and other participants were still detained.
Ohio State University disputes DOJ finding that medical school discriminates in admissions
Ohio State University said on Wednesday it disagreed with the US Department of Justice's findings that alleged its medical school favored Black and Hispanic applicants in admissions and discriminated against white and Asian applicants. The DOJ said findings from a federal probe showed Ohio State College of Medicine discriminated against white and Asian students in granting admission to its 2023, 2024 and 2025 incoming classes.
Trump warns Kansans that US will 'burn' like France if Democrats win
US President Donald Trump on Monday used violent unrest in France as an argument against Democrats in his battle to defend a Kansas Senate seat long held by Republicans but in danger of falling to his political opponents. Trump's rally on behalf of Republican incumbent Roger Marshall was his latest foray into conservative states where Republican candidates are on defense due to voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices.
New Mexico sues to stop payouts to Jeffrey Epstein's lawyer, accountant
New Mexico has filed a civil lawsuit to block payments from Jeffrey Epstein's estate to the late sex offender's lawyer and accountant, and to recover damages for survivors of his alleged sexual abuse, the state's top law enforcement official said on Wednesday. The suit is the first law enforcement action against Epstein's longtime personal attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn, according to New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez.
Trump to rally for Graham in tight South Carolina Senate race amid Russia rift
President Donald Trump travels to South Carolina on Wednesday to bolster Republican Darline Graham in a surprisingly competitive Senate race, even as his recent moves toward Russia have put him at odds with the sister of his late ally Lindsey Graham. Less than two weeks before the November 3 election, Darline Graham is running about even in the polls against Democrat Annie Andrews in a state Republicans typically win handily, another sign of the political headwinds confronting Trump's party amid high gasoline prices and the war in Iran.
Trump administration says it has revoked over 300,000 visas
President Donald Trump's administration has revoked over 300,000 US visas during his second term, the State Department said on Tuesday as the federal government continues its sweeping immigration crackdown. The number showed an acceleration in the pace of visa revocations in recent weeks.
Vance defends Ramaswamy's explosive attack ad in Ohio governor race
US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday defended an explosive attack ad by Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign against his Democratic rival in the Ohio governor’s race. The ad features Democrat Amy Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, disputing Acton’s account of a childhood she says involved a period of homelessness and sexual abuse. Arthur, whom Acton says she has not seen since 1978, urges Ohioans not to vote for her daughter.
Trump says fraud investigations make 'very big dent' in overseas scams
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday his administration has made a "very big dent" in scams by foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent investments, focusing on an anti-fraud message ahead of November's midterm elections. Trump, members of his cabinet and other top administration officials met at the White House for an event on cybercrime prevention, where FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency had taken down 20 scam compounds throughout the world.
Lawmakers say US briefing showed Russia targeting Democrats with misinformation
The top Democratic lawmakers on the congressional intelligence committees on Wednesday said they received an intelligence briefing that Russia has been waging a misinformation campaign against Democrats running in next month's midterm elections. The comments by Senator Mark Warner and Representative Jim Himes come as Republican President Donald Trump has in recent weeks eased economic sanctions on Russia and increased pressure on Ukraine to end its fight against Russian forces.
Supreme Court won't allow Trump administration restrictions on transgender inmates
The US Supreme Court rejected on Wednesday a bid by President Donald Trump's administration to immediately enforce a policy restricting gender-affirming care for transgender inmates in federal prisons in a rare win for transgender rights at the nation's top judicial body. The court denied the Justice Department's emergency request to lift a federal judge's order blocking the Federal Bureau of Prisons from implementing the policy, while a legal challenge to the measure plays out.
Explainer-Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections
President Donald Trump’s record-low popularity, voter frustration over the cost of living and a fierce immigration fight are shaping the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats gain the power to challenge his administration. Republicans hold narrow majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of each chamber.
US single-family housing starts plunge; building permits hit 3-1/2-year low
US single-family homebuilding fell sharply in September and permits for future construction tumbled to a 3-1/2-year low as higher mortgage rates suppressed demand, suggesting residential investment resumed its declining trend in the third quarter. The report from the Commerce Department on Tuesday followed on the heels of a National Association of Home Builders survey on Monday showing sentiment among single-family homebuilders plunged in October to the lowest level since June 2012.
Trump's MAGA Inc unleashes $277 million last-ditch effort to save Republicans in key US races
President Donald Trump has unleashed more than $277 million in a last-minute TV and direct mail advertising blitz over the final six weeks of the midterm campaign to help struggling Republican candidates in several races that are key to the party's chances to retain control of the US Congress. Trump's MAGA Inc super PAC, which has spent over $300 million on the midterms so far, poured the most money directly or through other PACs into the Texas, Michigan and Ohio Senate races where the Republican candidates are in tight races and trailing Democratic challengers in most polls, Federal Election Commission data shows.
The races that will decide control of the US Senate
Democrats need to pick up at least four seats in November's midterm elections to win control of the 100-seat US Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority. That was seen as unlikely at the beginning of the year, but President Donald Trump's unpopularity and voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices have made many races competitive even in states that he won handily in 2024. Here are the races that will determine control of the Senate:
US aims to loan about a third of heating oil reserve in bid to tame prices
The Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the 1-million-barrel US emergency heating oil reserve, the Department of Energy said on Wednesday, in a bid to tame surging prices. The move, reported first by Reuters, came after senators from both political parties urged the administration to release heating oil from the reserve.
How the Republican redistricting gambit faltered under Trump slump
At President Donald Trump's urging, Republicans pursued an unprecedented mid-decade redistricting campaign ahead of November's midterm elections, redrawing dozens of US House of Representatives districts in an effort to preserve their narrow majority. With less than two weeks until Election Day, however, Trump's unpopularity has wiped out most of those gains, leaving Republicans scrambling to defend even districts they engineered to be safely conservative.
Russia frees retired US schoolteacher in goodwill gesture as Putin meets Witkoff
Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired US schoolteacher in custody since 2022, from prison on Wednesday and took him to St Petersburg to fly back to the United States, after talks that Washington said were a step toward ending the war in Ukraine. Russian President Vladimir Putin made the announcement at a meeting in St Petersburg with US envoy Steve Witkoff, who later said the talks will continue toward planned technical-level discussions involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
Republicans fly past former spending caps nixed by US Supreme Court
Since the US Supreme Court in June struck down federal caps on political party spending with input from candidates, Republican committees have surged past the former limits by more than $126 million while their Democratic counterparts have topped them by more than $46 million ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans are seeking to retain control of Congress in the midterms. Coordinated spending by Republican and Democratic committees from July through September was nearly eight times what they spent during the same months of the last midterm elections in 2022.
Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty to New Mexico in data privacy case
A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history. The ruling came in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data.
Monitoring the monitors: US states prepare for surge of Justice Dept election watchers
When Justice Department staffers arrived in Minnesota this summer to monitor the state's primary election, they found themselves under scrutiny as well. Minnesota officials deployed about 40 state employees, working in pairs, to track the DOJ lawyers as they traveled through two counties during the August vote. The monitoring effort reflected mounting tensions between Minnesota and the Trump administration over elections and immigration. Democratic Secretary of State Steve Simon said his office is likely to continue coordinating with the state attorney general's office to shadow federal monitors during the November 3 midterms, when control of Congress is at stake. California has launched a similar program.
Pennsylvania measles cases rise to 1,317, state health department says
The Pennsylvania Department of Health on Wednesday reported 1,317 measles cases in the state, up 31 cases since its previous update on Monday, as the outbreak of the highly contagious disease continued. Pennsylvania has confirmed measles cases in 43 counties, with Washington County added to the list of affected counties.
US busts ring accused of arranging hundreds of sham marriages in Massachusetts
Federal prosecutors on Wednesday charged six people with participating in a long-running scheme to allegedly arrange hundreds of sham marriages in Massachusetts in order to help immigrants unlawfully obtain green cards and potential US citizenship. US Attorney Leah Foley during a press conference in Boston said the scheme's alleged mastermind, Jennifer Gonzalez, helped organize sham marriages for over a decade in Massachusetts, a Democratic-led state the defendant described as a "sanctuary" jurisdiction where "you get a lot of help as an immigrant."
Trump, in North Carolina, says Republicans will defy midterm odds
With his approval rating at record lows, President Donald Trump attempted to defy political gravity in a pep rally in North Carolina on Tuesday, urging voters to support his favored Senate candidate in a race some Republican groups have already given up on. Trump has embarked on a campaign blitz ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, traveling more than 29,000 miles (46,671 km) since late September to boost Republican candidates. His second stop in North Carolina in as many months was a signal of how much is at stake in this southern state.
US high court rulings have been 'destructive to democracy,' Justice Kagan says
US Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan on Tuesday said the court's conservative majority has undermined democracy and "created a race to the bottom" in how congressional districts are drawn. Kagan, one of the court's three liberals, told students at Catholic University's law school that the conservatives have enabled increased political polarization by not reining in partisan gerrymandering, which involves states redrawing the boundaries of electoral districts based on the partisan leanings of voters to boost a political party's candidates.
Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen released by Russia?
President Vladimir Putin announced the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russian detention on Wednesday, at the start of talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff. Here are details of Hubbard's case:WHO IS STEPHEN HUBBARD?
US Agriculture Dept confirms first detection of New World screwworm in US wildlife
The US Department of Agriculture said on Wednesday it has confirmed the first detection of flesh-eating parasite New World screwworm in US wildlife in an elk in Pecos County, Texas. The elk was located on a game ranch and was reported after being harvested by a hunter, the USDA said in a statement.
Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centers popular
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies building data centers should pay a "dividend" to the communities where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular. "I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social post.
US agents investigate report incendiary device thrown at ICE office in Atlanta
US federal agents are investigating reports that an incendiary device was thrown at the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) building in downtown Atlanta, Georgia, on Tuesday night. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) personnel and evidence response technicians are on site collecting evidence, the agency's Atlanta public affairs department said in an emailed statement.
Trump asks US Supreme Court to allow Big Bend border wall construction
President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Wednesday to let it proceed with a plan to build a US-Mexico border barrier in a remote region in West Texas that includes Big Bend National Park. The Justice Department filed an emergency request for the court to lift a federal judge's order halting wall construction in the region while a lawsuit against the project brought by an environmental group and other challengers plays out.
After generations in Central Park, horse-drawn carriages face a ban
To observers, the horse-drawn carriages driven by coachmen in black top hats, ferrying passengers through Central Park and nearby Manhattan streets, can seem like relics from another time. They soon may be.
