items.title: BMO is ‘leaning into’ the defence industry
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: BMO is expanding its focus on defence as the government looks to spend more in the sector as part of its broader build Canada agenda.
items.body: BMO is expanding its focus on defence as the government looks to spend more in the sector as part of its broader build Canada agenda. Darryl White, BMO Financial Group CEO, said that the lender is “responding to the signal” from Canada’s federal government amid commitments to raise defence spending. White said the bank has a long history of operating in the defence industry while serving small and large domestic firms. “We’re taking a strength of ours (and) leaning into it even more heavily than we were before,” he said. BMO said in a news release Wednesday that it will co-host a defence forum in Toronto with the Institute of International Finance on Thursday. The bank said it will involve bringing finance leaders from the Canadian defence industry to discuss opportunities and challenges. The announcement marks another step in BMO honing in on defence. In September, BMO announced plans to mobilize up to $70 billion in new capital over 10 years for key sectors of Canada’s economy, including defence. Other sectors included infrastructure for electricity, energy and transportation as well as oil and gas, mining and AI. Other large banks have made similar moves. CIBC has committed $2 billion to support small and medium-sized defence businesses with dual uses in the civilian sector. Meanwhile, TD Bank committed $150 billion over five years to accelerate investment in key industries including defence. In February, BMO announced it had joined the international Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB). The bank, spearheaded by NATO countries, is meant to reduce borrowing costs for military spending by pooling credit strength. All of Canada’s Big Six banks have put their support behind the DSRB. In an October report, BMO economists forecast that Canada’s pledge to spend five per cent of annual GDP on defence by 2035 would generate about $150 billion in annual economic impact by that year. “We haven’t seen something that can singularly deliver that much economic impact in this country in a very long time,” White said, adding that he is optimistic it can be achieved. “Do I think that the probability of getting there is high? Yes, I do because if you look on whether it’s the procurement side of things or the infrastructure side of things, there are commitments that I believe will be kept and we expect to play a very big part of that.” BMO’s moves come after hundreds of executives and global asset managers assembled in Toronto in September for Canada’s first national investment summit. Prime Minister Mark Carney had set an ambitious goal of attracting $1 trillion in new investment to Canada over the next five years. White said that foreign investment sentiment in Canada has changed. “I’ve been watching this for a very long time … over the course of the last couple of years international investors have gotten themselves closer and closer to getting on the field for participation in Canadian investment,” he said. “The summit, I think was a was a nexus where we could bring people as close to the field as you can get.” However, he said summits are generally not where deals get done. “There’s a little bit of romanticizing that goes on around people have summits and cut deals. That’s not really the way it works,” he said. White said it’s a place where people develop more relationships, get themselves closer to the interest in investing, but deals come when the conditions are right and the term sheets start to flow. “I don’t think we’re there yet, but we’ve certainly done a good job laying more groundwork than we have otherwise.” Another sign that BMO is increasing its footprint in the industry was the appointment of Michael Bonner as the enterprise chair of its Canadian defence sector segment. Bonner will also act as a liaison to government agencies and industry associations regarding defence-related financing, export credit, and procurement. “BMO has the experience, expertise and relationships to help clients of all sizes capitalize on that growth,” Bonner said in a news release. White’s comments come as he is scheduled to speak at the Toronto Global Forum on Wednesday. “It brings together leaders from around the world that are shaping their economies and an ability therefore to share best practices against the geopolitical realignment that we’ve got,” he said. Some of the major themes are AI, energy, infrastructure, finance and defence. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 21, 2026. Daniel Johnson, The Canadian Press

items.title: ロシアの米国向け軽油タンカー第1便、22日出航＝副首相
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] - ロシアのノバク副首相は２１日、トランプ米大統領との軽油供給合意を受け、米国向け軽油を積んだ最初のタンカーが２２日に出航すると明らかにした。現地紙ベドモスチが報じた。

報道によると、ノバク氏はタンカーに軽油４万トンを積み込むと述べ、供給に関する書類の手続きも完了が近いと説明した。積み出し港は明らかにしなかった。

ロシア通信（ＲＩＡ）によると、ノバク氏は「当然追加の出荷も続く。両首脳の間で合意が成立している。可能な範囲で米国の需要に応える」と述べた。

トランプ氏はこれまでに、ロシアが直ちに３０万トン（２２５万バレル）を輸出し、１１月に５０万トン、「その直後」に１００万トンを輸出すると説明している。

プーチン大統領は２１日、サンクトペテルブルクで米国のウィットコフ中東担当特使と会談した。ウィットコフ氏はロシアが９日に軽油の輸出禁止を解除したことに謝意を示した。プーチン氏も軽油輸出合意に言及し、合意後に世界の軽油価格が５─６％下落したと述べた。

ウィットコフ氏はテレビで放映された発言で「これはわれわれが協力している一例だ。そのことに感謝したい」と述べた。

プーチン氏は軽油を積んだロシアの最初のタンカーが２─３日後に出港するとの見通しを示した。「現在、数隻のタンカーによる輸送を準備している。順次出港する。資金面の手当てが必要だ」と語った。またロシアは米国市場に肥料を「大量に」供給することも可能だと述べた。

Russia says it will send first diesel cargo to US on Thursday

Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on diesel exports on Oct 9, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after reaching the deal with US President Donald Trump to supply diesel to global markets.

MOSCOW: Russia will dispatch its first tanker with diesel for the United States on Thursday (Oct 22), Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said, according to the Vedomosti news outlet, after a deal with US President Donald Trump.
Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on diesel exports on Oct 9, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after reaching the deal with Trump to supply diesel to global markets.
Novak said on Wednesday the vessel will carry 40,000 metric tons of the fuel, adding that the paperwork on the fuel supply is nearing its completion, according to media reports. He did not name the port from which the cargo will be delivered.
"Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States' needs, to the extent of our capabilities," RIA news agency quoted Novak as saying.

Trump has said Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter".
The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day.
Russian President Vladimir Putin was hosting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday, after the US-Russia diesel export deal led to a sharp deterioration in ties between the United States and Ukraine.
During the talks in St Petersburg, Witkoff thanked Putin for lifting the export restrictions. Putin also mentioned the deal, saying that global diesel prices dropped by 5 per cent to 6 per cent after the agreement.
"That's an example of us working together, I want to thank you for that," Witkoff said in televised comments.
Putin also said that first Russian tankers with diesel will departs in two to three days.
"We are preparing deliveries of several vessels, the tankers, right now. They will go one after another. The financial component should be provided," he said, adding that Russia also would be able to supply fertilisers in "large quantities" to the US market.

items.title: GSK is two shots away from clean bill of health
items.author: Aimee Donnellan
items.creator: Aimee Donnellan
items.summary: One of Europe’s most cheaply valued drugmakers, the £75 bln group run by Luke Miels is turning a corner. Fears over expiring patents are easing thanks to a booming oncology unit. A £40 bln sales target looks hard, but Miels may fix that with canny dealmaking and luck in the lab.
items.body:
If GSK (GSK.L) were a patient doctors would be starting to hope that it’s on the mend. Despite being one of the cheapest of the global pharma stocks, new CEO Luke Miels is ploughing money into research and development and doing savvy deals. The big question is can he deliver on his target of over £40 billion in sales by 2031 .
Signs of a recovery have appeared slowly. When Miels’ predecessor Emma Walmsley was in charge, she spun out the consumer goods business which makes Sensodyne toothpaste, now called Haleon (HLN.L) . Investors hoped the surgery would unleash a leaner, less indebted business that could focus its efforts on dealmaking and its core areas of vaccines, HIV and general medicines including inhalers and antibiotics. So far, that's yet to translate into a material valuation bump: GSK trades at around 10 times forward earnings, in line with its multiple when Haleon was spun off in 2022 , and below peers like AstraZeneca (AZN.L) , Novartis (NOVN.S) and Roche (ROPC.S) .
The main reason is fear of what comes next. Dolutegravir, GSK’s star HIV treatment which accounted for 17% of GSK’s near £33 billion of sales last year, loses patent protection in the US from 2028. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha expect revenue in that division to halve by 2031. Vaccines have also lost steam. Anti vaccine sentiment is growing in the US, and analysts expect the division to grow sales by an average of less than 2% over the next five years.
However, Miels is plugging these holes partly by bolstering the group’s growing cancer business. Last year, sales in oncology rose by over 40% to nearly £2 billion and they are expected to reach over £5 billion pounds by 2031. And he’s hoping to boost that further through deals and in-house drug development. In June, he splurged [USN:L6N42H0KM TEXT:"$11 billion"] on US lung cancer specialist Nuvalent. The business won regulatory approval for one of its drugs a month after the deal was announced and GSK is expecting to hear about another remedy later this year. This week GSK won regulatory backing for a new rectal cancer drug. Growth in GSK’s oncology business should help offset the decline in HIV as dolutegravir's patents expire.
The cancer success isn't the only sign that GSK's plan to boost in-house drug development is paying off. Miels is expecting to start over 20 new late stage drug trials this year. Potential blockbuster drugs include a hepatitis B remedy bepirovirsen which it reckons will generate £2 billion in annual sales. Berenberg analysts estimate the group's likely return on research investment is now over 10%, healthily exceeding the sector's 8% cost of capital.
GSK is still some way off hitting Miels' target to reach £40 billion of sales by 2031. But the gap is closing: Analysts polled by Visible Alpha estimate sales of £37 billion that year, up from less than £34 billion a year ago. To hit the magic number, Miels will probably need to do more small deals, as well as keep securing fresh drug approvals. But the danger that he will resort to more large risky takeovers is probably easing. That, along with GSK's broader turnaround, means its valuation should start to catch up with its healthier peers.
Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn .
GSK will unveil its third quarter earnings on October 28.
The US Food and Drug Administration on October 19 approved GSK’s Jemperli, an immunotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer.

Elon Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger would be a ‘good idea’. Committees formed to explore deal

SpaceX is valued at $2 trillion and Tesla at $1.5 trillion. A merger would create one of the largest corporate combinations in history.

Purvi Rajpuria

New Delhi: Elon Musk on Tuesday said that a merger between his two biggest companies, SpaceX and Tesla, would be a “good idea.” 

While the tech billionaire warned that it would be premature to assume the certainty of the merger, he confirmed that special committees had been formed within both companies to examine the move.

Musk has suggested the possibility of a merger between the two companies in the past as well, citing growing overlap between their operations. Last week, British bank Barclays also floated the suggestion that a merger could be announced before Tesla’s annual meeting in December. 

Show Full Article

Stock prices for both companies went up after the comment. While shares of SpaceX rose 8 per cent, Tesla’s shares rose 1.8 per cent. The space tech company had also posted its first profit as a public company in the third quarter of this year. 

Tesla, an electric car company, is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion. SpaceX, which manufactures space rockets and Starlink internet satellites, is valued at $2 trillion. A combination of the two companies would mark one of the largest mergers in history. 

‘Merit in combining the companies’
Musk recently launched Terafab, a combined effort to manufacture computer chips between SpaceX and Tesla. Additionally, SpaceX acquired X and xAI earlier this year, before it went public. Both these moves point to Musk’s attempts at consolidating his companies, signalling that he sees them as operating more effectively when working together. 

A full merger between SpaceX and Tesla would make sense considering both companies do work around chips, artificial intelligence, software and more, the BBC reported .

“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starlink constellation, connectivity,” Musk said.     

The merger, however, would ultimately be decided by shareholders. At least 50 per cent of Tesla’s shareholders would need to approve the merger—something Musk has described as “quite a high hurdle to achieve”.

Also read: Ali G is outdated—and that’s why he’s back, writes Sacha Baron Cohen in TIME

Benefits of the merger?
With Musk owning just under half of SpaceX and nearly a fifth of Tesla, analysts have said that a merger would give him control of the combined entity, Reuters reported . 

Justus Parmar, Chief Executive Officer at Fortuna Investments, pointed to another benefit of bringing SpaceX and Tesla together in one place, for investors to back.  

“Tesla runs a high-margin, cash-generative automotive business and there’s more growth to come with the robotaxis on the way. That cash flow could help support SpaceX’s bottom line and fund its very capital-intensive space exploration and launch goals, including orbital data centers,” he said .

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

items.title: Nigeria reports Ebola case as outbreak reaches West Africa
items.author: Elisha Bala-Gbogbo, Camillus Eboh
items.creator: Elisha Bala-Gbogbo, Camillus Eboh
items.summary: Nigeria reported its first Ebola case in more than a decade on Tuesday, becoming the fourth African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that health officials have described as the fastest-spreading on record.
items.body:
Nigeria reported its first Ebola case in more than a decade on Tuesday, becoming the fourth African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that health officials have described as the [USN:L6N4421DF TEXT:"fastest-spreading on record"].
The Ebola species behind the outbreak kills about half of those infected and has no approved treatment or vaccine. Since the first cases were confirmed in Democratic Republic of Congo in May, the disease has killed 4,646 people. Health officials fear misinformation and [USN:L8N45M12L TEXT:"funding shortfalls"] could fuel further spread within the region and across borders.
Cases have also been reported in Uganda and, more recently, Kenya. "Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa. The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level," Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Director General Jean Kaseya said on X on Wednesday.
The Nigerian case involves a Ugandan woman who arrived in Nigeria's capital Abuja via Addis Ababa on October 5, Odianosen Ehiakhamen of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control told Arise TV on Tuesday.
She began feeling unwell two days later and sought treatment at a private hospital in Abuja on October 11 with malaria-like symptoms, but her condition did not improve, Ehiakhamen said.
CONCERN OF 'PAN-AFRICAN EVENT' After health officials learned she had recently travelled to Uganda, one of the countries affected by the current outbreak, they tested her for Ebola on October 19. The positive result was confirmed on Tuesday.
"My concern, now that this has spread from East Africa to West Africa, is that we now have a pan-African event, as opposed to a few at-risk countries," said Ayoade Alakija, a Nigerian physician who co-chairs a G7 committee for investment in global health.
Alakija also noted that it had taken 12 days since the woman fell sick for her to be tested for Ebola, potentially exposing many other people to the infection.
"Abuja is one of Africa's main cities ... with air and road connections daily, multiple, across the world. It’s a very different prospect – and that's what worries me — the amount of time it took."
Nigerian authorities have identified 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers. They include the patient's husband, a Swiss national who lives with her in Abuja.
Officials are also tracing passengers who travelled with her from Uganda to Nigeria but do not believe she was symptomatic during the flight.
Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate told public broadcaster NTA that the woman was in isolation and receiving treatment.
UGANDA SAYS IT HAS NO ACTIVE EBOLA CASES Uganda's health ministry said the woman had travelled to Congo, where more than 9,500 Ebola cases have been recorded across eight provinces.
It was not immediately clear where she had been in Congo, and Nigerian authorities have not confirmed that she had visited the country.
"Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here," Uganda's health ministry said, adding that the country has no active Ebola cases.
Uganda reported 20 cases in May and June, mostly imported from Congo, but the World Health Organization declared the country [USN:L6N44N0VL TEXT:"Ebola-free"] in August.
Earlier this month, Kenya reported its first Ebola case, involving a traveller who arrived from Congo via Uganda. The country has since reported [USN:L1N4660OP TEXT:"nine cases"], all linked to the same patient.
The spread of Ebola to Kenya raised questions about the effectiveness of [USN:L6N45S157 TEXT:"border screening systems"] designed to prevent cross-border transmission.
Pate, Nigeria's health minister, said the country had successfully contained Ebola in 2014 during the West African epidemic, the largest outbreak on record.
He said Nigeria had the systems in place to respond to the new case.

That typically means scheduling my appointment for sometime in mid-to-late October.

items.summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks while weakness in communication services stocks capped gains.
items.body:
The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks while weakness in communication services stocks capped gains.
SpaceX shares (SPCX.O) finished up 7.8% after Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm posted its first profit as a public company. Musk said, following the report, that [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a merger of SpaceX"] and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea," also boosting Tesla shares.
Elsewhere in earnings, Super Micro (SMCI.O) shares jumped 9.6% and it was among the S&P 500's top gainers after the AI server maker [USN:L4N4661QH TEXT:"forecast"] quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. The report also benefited peers HPE (HPE.N) , which rose 3.7%, and Dell (DELL.N) , which rose 5.3%.
The reports provided some reassurance to investors who have been worried about the sustainability of massive spending on AI buildouts and their profitability. The technology sector was hammered last week by a selloff in AI-linked stocks, with data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) at the center of the storm.
The SpaceX news "pushes back on some of the investor worries" about AI along with some help from Super Micro, according to Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones.
Kourkafas said the reports will not "answer all the questions investors have on returns on AI investments, but it's a good start."
As a result, the S&P 500 Information Technology index (.SPLRCT) finished up 1.6%, the biggest gainer among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors.
"It's really a positive technology story for almost anyone that is somewhat involved in the artificial intelligence ecosystem," said Marc Dizard, chief investment officer at Huntington Bank.
"The technology market reaction has been a reaffirmation that the artificial intelligence trade is still intact," he added.
However, Dizard said sentiment can quickly shift around AI and that investors will seek reaffirmation when they monitor earnings reports from other companies.
Shares in [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"Meta"] (META.O) rose 3% in late trading after it released its quarterly results following the regular session's close. After finishing up 3.4% in the regular session, [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"Tesla"] shares rose another 1.6% following its report, which was also issued after the close.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 360.21 points, or 0.69%, to 52,856.09, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 44.60 points, or 0.58%, to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 278.04 points, or 1.05%, to 26,702.86.
Within technology, one of the strongest areas was chips with a 2% rally in the Philadelphia Semiconductor index (.SOX) , which has had a volatile month so far including an eight-session selloff.
Gains in the benchmark S&P 500 were limited however by a 1.3% decline in communication services stocks (.SPLRCL) . The biggest losers included telecom operators such as AT&T (T.N) , which sank 6.5% even as it beat [USN:L4N4670UN TEXT:"third-quarter"] revenue and profit expectations.
The SpaceX results, along with a recent wireless spectrum purchase, fanned fears that it could become a formidable competitor in telecoms, according to Dizard. T-Mobile US (TMUS.O) shares fell 2.5% and Verizon Communications (VZ.N) lost 2.2%.
Also in communications services, Netflix (NFLX.O) shares sank 5.3% after the video streaming company issued [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"a weaker-than-expected forecast"] for its fourth-quarter profit. Google's parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) also declined 1.6%.
Abbott Laboratories (ABT.N) shares dropped 1.9% after the medical device maker cut its [USN:L4N4670ZJ TEXT:"2026 sales growth forecast"].
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.37-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 131 new highs and 221 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 2,690 stocks rose and 2,068 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.3-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 26 new 52-week highs and 3 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 53 new highs and 216 new lows.
On US exchanges roughly 16.11 billion shares changed hands compared with the 17.10 billion average for the last 20 sessions.

items.title: ロシア、米国人元教師を解放　米特使とプーチン氏が会談
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [サンクトペテルブルク（ロシア）　２１日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[サンクトペテルブルク（ロシア）　２１日　ロイター] - ロシアは２１日、２０２２年から拘束していた元教師の米国人スティーブン・ハバード氏（７４）を刑務所から解放し、米国への帰国便に搭乗させるためサンクトペテルブルクに移送した。ミシガン州出身のハバード氏は、非公開の裁判で雇い兵活動を行ったとして有罪判決を受け、ロシアで７年近くの刑に服していた。

ロシアのプーチン大統領は、サンクトペテルブルクでトランプ米政権のウィットコフ中東担当特使と会談した際に解放を発表。ウィットコフ氏はその後、予定される米国、ロシア、ウクライナの実務者協議に向けて話し合いを続けると述べた。

ウィットコフ氏は解放に謝意を示す中で、プーチン氏を「人道主義者」と呼び、米共和、民主両党の議員から厳しい批判を浴びた。トランプ大統領は最近、ロシア産軽油の購入合意や新たな制裁の適用免除など、ロシアに歩み寄る姿勢を示しており、米議会で超党派の反発を招き、欧州各国政府にも懸念が広がっている。

ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官は、プーチン氏がトランプ氏の要請を受けてハバード氏を解放したと述べ、同氏の健康状態も考慮したと説明した。トランプ氏もその後、数日前の電話会談で解放を要請し、プーチン氏が応じたと明らかにした。

国営テレビで放映された会談で、ウィットコフ氏はプーチン氏に対し「（トランプ）大統領も、国民全体も、ハバード氏の件について感謝の意を示している」とし、「あなたのおかげで彼は家族のもとに帰ることができる」と述べた。

ロイターに提供された動画には、濃い色のフリースを着てひげをきれいにそったハバード氏が、ロシア国内の非公開の場所でウィットコフ氏と握手し、謝意を示す様子が映っていた。トランプ氏はその後、米国旗を手にして機内にいるとみられるハバード氏の写真を投稿した。 

ハバード氏の息子ジョセフ・コールマン氏はロイターへの音声メッセージで、父親がロシアで飛行機に搭乗する前に短時間、電話で話したと明らかにした。「きょうは足取りも軽そうで、声に幸せがにじんでいた」と語った。

＜３カ国協議を計画＞

ウィットコフ氏はプーチン氏との協議を「建設的」と評価。Ｘへの投稿で、戦争終結を目指すトランプ氏の取り組みを進めるため、オスロでウクライナと欧州の首脳とも会談したと明らかにした。

ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、交渉担当者によるロシア、米国との３カ国協議をできるだけ早く、望ましくは１１月上旬までに開催するという米国の提案を支持すると述べた。

ウィットコフ氏と会談したノルウェーのストーレ首相はこれに先立ち、協議は１１月中旬に開かれる公算が大きく、紛争終結後の安全保障体制の可能性に焦点を当てると述べていた。

一方、ウクライナの首都キーウの当局者らは２１日夜、ロシア軍が首都を弾道ミサイルで攻撃し、住宅やガソリンスタンドが損傷したほか、負傷者が出たと明らかにした。

＜「人道主義者」との称賛に批判＞

ハバード氏の解放を巡るウィットコフ氏のプーチン氏称賛に対し、米政界の一部から批判が上がった。共和党のトム・ティリス上院議員はＸへの投稿で「『人道主義者』の定義を調べてみるべきだ。なんと恥ずべき、言語道断の発言か」と記した。

トランプ氏はホワイトハウスで記者団からウィットコフ氏の「人道主義者」発言について問われ、「その点、つまり一生刑務所にいると思っていた男性を釈放したという意味では、そう言えるだろう。ただ、私からはどちらとも言わない」と述べた。

また、米国は解放の「見返りに何も提供していない」とし、戦争の終結に「近づいている」と述べた。

ハバード氏については「彼は誰よりも幸せだ。本人には非常に驚きだったが、私が実現させた。実際には先週末のプーチン大統領との電話会談で決まったことで、われわれは非常に感謝している。家族も大変喜んでいる」と語った。

ハバード氏は２２年４月、ウクライナ東部のイジューム市で逮捕された。ロシア検察当局は、同氏が同地でウクライナ軍の検問所の警備にあたっていたと主張していた。

ロシア国営メディアは、ハバード氏が起訴内容について有罪を認めたと報じた。しかし、米国を拠点とする同氏の弁護士マーティン・デ・ルカ氏は以前、ロイターに対し、ハバード氏から「自分に対する罪状は虚偽であり、いかなる戦闘部隊や軍事部隊にも所属していなかった」と伝えられていたことを明らかにしている。

items.title: Why Musk backs a $3.5 trillion Tesla-SpaceX merger and what it means
items.summary: Elon Musk has backed a potential $3.5 trillion merger of SpaceX and Tesla, aiming to combine their AI, robotics, satellite and energy businesses, though regulatory and governance risks remain.
items.body:
Home / World News / Why Musk backs a $3.5 trillion Tesla-SpaceX merger and what it means

Why Musk backs a $3.5 trillion Tesla-SpaceX merger and what it means Elon Musk has backed a potential $3.5 trillion merger of SpaceX and Tesla, aiming to combine their AI, robotics, satellite and energy businesses, though regulatory and governance risks remain.

Elon Musk has backed a potential merger of Tesla and SpaceX that could create a company worth about $3.5 trillion, combining businesses spanning AI, robotics, energy and space technology. (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 21 2026 | 10:46 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Elon Musk believes a merger between Tesla and SpaceX is a good idea, he said on Tuesday, ??publicly backing an idea that would create one of the most valuable companies in the world, worth about $3.5 trillion.
While electric-vehicle maker Tesla and rocket company SpaceX were once seen as largely separate businesses, the lines between them have blurred as Musk expands into artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced manufacturing, ??satellite communications, and computing infrastructure, including data centers on Earth and potentially in orbit.
  Here's what a potential merger could mean:
  WHY WOULD MUSK DO THIS?   A merger would create a single company at the center of Musk's long-term vision: an integrated technology and manufacturing empire spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications, and transportation on Earth and beyond.
 

  "I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation (of orbital data centers), connectivity," Musk said on Tuesday.
Also Read

Musk says Tesla-SpaceX merger being considered, special committees formed

Musk ordered slowdown of Starlink service used by Ukraine's military

Tesla shareholders to vote on Musk's re-election, $158 bn pay on Dec 3

Elon Musk says he will gift SpaceX shares to 'every kid in America'

OpenAI poaches another SpaceX sales lead for cybersecurity business

  Bringing the companies together could also simplify decision-making. Many of Musk's projects already cut across multiple companies, requiring approvals from separate boards and shareholders. A combined company would give management more freedom to deploy capital, engineering talent and infrastructure where it sees the greatest opportunity.
  Musk has long argued that he needs greater influence over Tesla to pursue its AI and robotics strategy. He owns nearly a fifth of   Tesla and holds voting control at SpaceX. A merger could consolidate his influence.

  WHAT DOES IT MEAN FOR INVESTORS?   Tesla shareholders would gain access to SpaceX's rapidly growing Starlink broadband operation, launch services business and future space ventures. SpaceX investors would gain ownership of Tesla's vehicle, energy storage, autonomous driving and robotics businesses.
  A merged company could also become one of the world's most valuable corporations, with a market value of about $3.5 trillion, combining leadership positions in automobiles, robotics, satellite communications, launch services, energy storage and AI infrastructure.
  Supporters would likely argue that the combined company could allocate capital more efficiently across businesses that are increasingly interdependent.
  Critics, however, argue that investors would be assuming exposure to a much broader range of technical, regulatory and execution risks, some of which have little connection to one another.

  WHERE COULD SPACEX AND TESLA WORK TOGETHER?   Starlink satellites could provide communications links for Tesla's robotaxis, autonomous systems and future generations of Optimus humanoid robots. Tesla's battery and energy-storage products could help support SpaceX's growing power needs, including future data-center projects.
  Musk has already announced one major Tesla-SpaceX collaboration, Terafab, a semiconductor and AI-computing project aimed at producing the advanced chips ??needed for Tesla's autonomous vehicles and Optimus robots, as well as SpaceX's AI and data-center ambitions. Musk hopes it can start volume production by late 2028.
  Tesla's expertise in large-scale factory automation could complement SpaceX's efforts to industrialize Starship production, while SpaceX technologies have already appeared in Tesla products, most notably the planned use of rocket-derived components in the next-generation Roadster.

  A merged company could also coordinate efforts to secure strategic supply chains, leveraging Tesla's scale in batteries, semiconductors and manufacturing equipment alongside SpaceX's demand for specialized metals, electronics, propulsion components and satellite hardware.
  WHAT ARE THE DOWNSIDE RISKS?   The biggest challenges may be geopolitics and regulation.
  SpaceX is a major contractor for the US military, intelligence agencies and NASA. Tesla, meanwhile, remains deeply tied to China through its Shanghai factory, which plays a major role in vehicle production and sales. That combination could invite heightened scrutiny from US regulators and national-security officials as well as from Beijing.
  The merger would also face shareholder and governance hurdles. Investors would need to be persuaded that combining two already complex businesses creates more value than keeping them separate. Questions about conflicts of interest, voting control and capital allocation would inevitably follow.

  Then there is execution risk. Starship, robotaxis, humanoid robots, AI data centers, mobile communications and orbital infrastructure are all expensive, technically challenging bets. Combining Tesla and SpaceX would not reduce those risks. It would simply place them under one roof.

items.title: Anthropic, music publishers square off on 'fair use' defense in AI copyright case
items.author: Blake Brittain
items.creator: Blake Brittain
items.summary: Anthropic urged a judge in California on Wednesday to rule that the AI company's use of millions of song lyrics to train its chatbot Claude is protected as "fair use" under US copyright law, as it seeks to scuttle a lawsuit brought by Universal Music Group and other music publishers.
items.body:
Anthropic urged a judge in California on Wednesday to rule that the AI company's use of millions of song lyrics to train its chatbot Claude is protected as "fair use" under US copyright law, as it seeks to scuttle a lawsuit brought by Universal Music Group (UMG.AS) and other music publishers.
US District Judge Eumi Lee did not rule at a hearing in San Jose but pressed both sides on the fair use question, which could be key to dozens of other high-stakes copyright infringement cases in the AI era.
Lee also questioned the publishers' assertion that Claude's ability to compose lyrics threatens the market for the publishers' lyrics.
Anthropic lawyer Sonal Mehta of WilmerHale argued that its AI training leads to the creation of transformative new content, putting it squarely under the fair use doctrine.
The publishers' attorney Matt Oppenheim of Oppenheim + Zebrak responded that Anthropic misuses its lyrics to generate competing content that harms human songwriters.
Oppenheim said Claude received nearly 120,000 requests to generate "synthetic" lyrics over a six-month period. He said large language models like Claude "could overwhelm the market with AI-generated content very easily."
Mehta countered that AI has not reduced demand for the lyrics, and that the publishers could not identify any specific instances of market harm from Claude or other large language models.
Mehta also said that UMG itself has said that AI is "overwhelmingly a net positive" for the music industry.
EARLY FAIR USE RULINGS Fair use could determine the fate of pending lawsuits brought by authors, news outlets, visual artists and others against tech giants including Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta Platforms over their AI training.
Two other Northern California judges who have already weighed in on the closely watched issue have split on whether generative AI training generally makes fair use of copyrighted material, which would shield tech companies from liability for using millions of copyrighted works to train their systems without content owners' permission.
Now-retired US District Judge William Alsup sided with [USN:L6N3S50SQ TEXT:"Anthropic"] last year on its argument that its AI training made fair use of books. Two days later, US District Judge Vince Chhabria [USN:L6N3S10OC TEXT:"ruled for Meta"] in a similar lawsuit but warned that AI training “in many circumstances” would not be fair use.
In the case being heard by Lee, music publishers UMG, Concord and ABKCO [USN:L1N3BO1X6 TEXT:"sued Anthropic"] in 2023, alleging its use of their lyrics to train Claude to respond to human prompts infringed their copyrights in hundreds of songs by artists including Beyonce, the Rolling Stones and the Beach Boys.
Anthropic [USN:L6N41418J TEXT:"has argued"] that its AI training makes transformative use of song lyrics to "help Claude understand human language and enable progress and productivity in science, business and education."

items.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、ＣＡＴＬ10％安　景気対策への期待後退
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Summer Zhen

[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に向けた大型景気刺激策への期待後退がセンチメントを圧迫した。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１％安で引け、２０２５年８月以来の安値となった。上海総合指数は０．６％安。

香港のハンセン指数は０．９％安。

ハンセンテック指数は、中国が市場下支えのために大規模な景気刺激策を導入した２０２４年９月以来の安値に沈んだ。

中国のバッテリー最大手
items.body:
Summer Zhen

[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に向けた大型景気刺激策への期待後退がセンチメントを圧迫した。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１％安で引け、２０２５年８月以来の安値となった。上海総合指数は０．６％安。

香港のハンセン指数は０．９％安。

ハンセンテック指数は、中国が市場下支えのために大規模な景気刺激策を導入した２０２４年９月以来の安値に沈んだ。

中国のバッテリー最大手 のＣＡＴＬ株は香港・本土市場ともに１０％超急落。競争激化と中国の自動車販売の伸び鈍化を受け、第３・四半期の利益成長が大幅に減速したと発表した。

玩具メーカー、ポップマートの業績不振もリスク回避姿勢を強めた。株価は２１日に５％下落。第３・四半期決算が失望視されるとと見込まれる中、今月１５％下げている。

市場関係者によると、投資家は第３・四半期の決算発表を前に、消費関連株の売買を通じて中国国内需要の弱さに対する弱気の見方を示している。経済成長が引き続き堅調な中、政策当局が早期に市場刺激策を打ち出す公算は小さいとみられている。

バークレイズはリポートで、輸出主導の産業が堅調なため引き続き内需の弱さを覆い隠していると指摘。「成長目標がほぼ達成されており、大規模な景気刺激策導入のハードルは高まったとみている」との見方を示した。

酒類と新エネルギー関連企業が下げを主導した一方、医薬品、通信、クラウドコンピューティング関連企業は相場をアウトパフォームした。

ジュリアス・ベアのエコノミスト、ソフィー・アルターマット氏はリポートで「政府の焦点は、短期的な成長押し上げよりも、技術進歩、産業の高度化、自給率の一段の向上に引き続き置かれている」と指摘した。

市場関係者によると、短期的にはより厳格な税制政策も株式相場の重しとなっている。

ロイターの報道によると、中国政府は富裕層に対し、海外信託関連の所得税を１０月２２日までに申告・納税するよう求めた。これを受け、現金確保のため株式を売却する動きが一部で広がっている。

中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、ＣＡＴＬ10％安　景気対策への期待後退
10/21 19:08 配信

Summer Zhen

[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に向けた大型景気刺激策への期待後退がセンチメントを圧迫した。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１％安で引け、２０２５年８月以来の安値となった。上海総合指数は０．６％安。

香港のハンセン指数は０．９％安。

ハンセンテック指数は、中国が市場下支えのために大規模な景気刺激策を導入した２０２４年９月以来の安値に沈んだ。

中国のバッテリー最大手 のＣＡＴＬ株は香港・本土市場ともに１０％超急落。競争激化と中国の自動車販売の伸び鈍化を受け、第３・四半期の利益成長が大幅に減速したと発表した。

玩具メーカー、ポップマートの業績不振もリスク回避姿勢を強めた。株価は２１日に５％下落。第３・四半期決算が失望視されるとと見込まれる中、今月１５％下げている。

市場関係者によると、投資家は第３・四半期の決算発表を前に、消費関連株の売買を通じて中国国内需要の弱さに対する弱気の見方を示している。経済成長が引き続き堅調な中、政策当局が早期に市場刺激策を打ち出す公算は小さいとみられている。

バークレイズはリポートで、輸出主導の産業が堅調なため引き続き内需の弱さを覆い隠していると指摘。「成長目標がほぼ達成されており、大規模な景気刺激策導入のハードルは高まったとみている」との見方を示した。

酒類と新エネルギー関連企業が下げを主導した一方、医薬品、通信、クラウドコンピューティング関連企業は相場をアウトパフォームした。

ジュリアス・ベアのエコノミスト、ソフィー・アルターマット氏はリポートで「政府の焦点は、短期的な成長押し上げよりも、技術進歩、産業の高度化、自給率の一段の向上に引き続き置かれている」と指摘した。

市場関係者によると、短期的にはより厳格な税制政策も株式相場の重しとなっている。

ロイターの報道によると、中国政府は富裕層に対し、海外信託関連の所得税を１０月２２日までに申告・納税するよう求めた。これを受け、現金確保のため株式を売却する動きが一部で広がっている。

小型株中心の深セン総合指数は０．４９％安、新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は１．６２％下落、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は０．０６％高。

items.title: Trump says fraud investigations make 'very big dent' in overseas scams
items.author: Courtney Rozen
items.creator: Courtney Rozen
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday his administration has made a "very big dent" in scams by foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent investments, focusing on an anti-fraud message ahead of November's midterm elections.
items.body:
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday his administration has made a "very big dent" in scams by foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent investments, focusing on an anti-fraud message ahead of November's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"].
Trump, members of his cabinet and other top administration officials met at the White House for an event on cybercrime prevention, where FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency had taken down 20 scam compounds throughout the world.
Early voting has already begun in many states ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, where Trump's Republican Party risks losing control of Congress while polls show that voters' top concern is the rising [USN:L6N44S0Y9 TEXT:"cost of living"].
"Federal law enforcement has been able to warn over 10,000 Americans targeted for victimization, and we've prevented $1.6 billion in losses — at least — this year," Trump said at the event.
Americans filed more than 1 million complaints with the FBI about internet scams last year, a 17% increase from 2024, according to an FBI report.
Cabinet officials at the meeting included Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche, while White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller were also present.
The president's team highlighted work to crack down on overseas crypto scams, with Miller saying that Trump "effectively declared cyber warfare against the cyber criminals."
Trump's family has been heavily involved in soliciting investments in crypto .
A Reuters investigation found the Republican president and his sons have added at least $2.3 billion to the family fortune from their main crypto ventures, while the investors they have wooed have taken a $2.3 billion hit.
White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly, in a statement to Reuters about its investigation, said: "All actions by President Trump and his administration are taken in the best interest of the American people."
Trump in October 2025 [USN:FWN3W42W4 TEXT:"pardoned"] Changpeng Zhao, the convicted founder of the Binance cryptocurrency exchange. Zhao quit his job after the [USN:L1N3CM1MQ TEXT:"company"] pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program.
In a March executive order, Trump directed the Justice Department to prioritize identifying and prosecuting scammers who carry out crimes online. Trump later directed the Department of Homeland Security to [USN:FWN4491P7 TEXT:"work"] with private companies to surveil foreign criminal hacking groups.

items.title: Booking.com targeted in EU investigation into phishing scams, fraudulent listings
items.author: Yun Chee Foo
items.creator: Yun Chee Foo
items.summary: EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday.
items.body:
EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday.
The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years.
Big online platforms are required to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content on their sites under the bloc's Digital Services Act, or risk fines of as much as 6% of their global annual turnover for violations.
Booking.com said it was engaging constructively with the Commission. "Security, trust and the protection of personal information are top priorities at Booking.com," a spokesperson for the company said.
"We remain committed to working with relevant governments, regulators, law enforcement and industry partners to combat cybercrime and online fraud, and protect travelers and partners."
The EU investigation will focus on fake listings — such as for non-existent properties — impersonation fraud and non-compliant accommodation offers, and whether Booking.com has properly identified, assessed and mitigated the systemic risks related to these.
Regulators will also look into phishing scams exploiting Booking.com's reservation and guest data shared with accommodation providers, the Commission said.
A third element will be paid-for boosted listings not clearly identifiable as advertisements. Booking.com is part of Booking Holdings (BKNG.O) .
"Europeans should be able to book their holidays without fear of being scammed," EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in a statement.
"The Digital Services Act sets clear responsibilities on platforms to address these risks, and we must ensure that the leading booking platform in Europe takes those responsibilities seriously," she said.

items.title: 中国奇瑞、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向き＝幹部
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [蕪湖（中国） ２１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[蕪湖（中国） ２１日 ロイター] - 中国の自動車大手、奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の幹部は２１日、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向きな姿勢を示した。「オモダ」「ジェクー」ブランドを展開する同社は欧州などで急成長しており、今後は北米での事業拡大を目指す。

バイスプレジデントのチャーリー・チャン氏は中国東部・蕪湖の本社でインタビューに応じ、２０２７年初めにカナダでブランドを立ち上げる準備を進めていることも明らかにした。

米国では１００％を超える関税やデータセキュリティー規制が障壁となり、中国の自動車メーカーは事実上締め出されている。

チャン氏は「米国については当然さまざまな選択肢を探っている」と述べ、柔軟に対応する姿勢を強調した。「米自動車メーカーとの提携の可能性も含め、さまざまな選択肢に非常に前向きだ」と語った。具体的にどのような提携を想定しているかは明らかにしなかった。

「技術面ではハードウエアもソフトウエアも中国製に頼らない方法を確実に見いだせる」と述べ、米国市場への参入に道筋をつけられるとの自信を示した。

items.author: CNA

Putin hosts Trump envoy for new Ukraine peace talks, frees US citizen held in Russia

Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US school teacher who had been held in Russia on mercenary charges, has been released.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev greets US special envoy Steve Witkoff upon his arrival at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg, Russia on Oct 21, 2026. (Photo: Reuters)

ST PETERSBURG, Russia: President Vladimir Putin hosted US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in a grand imperial palace on Wednesday (Oct 21) to review new ideas on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
The talks in St Petersburg , the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of a retired US school teacher held in Russia.
The encounter comes amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications.
The latest talks came more than two years since US President Donald Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours.

Witkoff flew into Russia's second city on Wednesday morning a day after conducting what a US official called "constructive" talks in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the leaders of Finland and Norway and European and NATO representatives, as President Donald Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing."
US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections.
Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system , though Zelenskyy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo, Norway on Oct 20, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/NTB/Heiko Junge)

STARLINK SPEEDS Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday that the problem lay with the terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Witkoff's meeting with Zelenskyy was positive and that Witkoff would share the results with Russia. He also reiterated that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink.
"He will now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and let's see if we can make some progress," he said.

Related:

Zelenskyy hails resumption of US advance warning of strikes on Ukraine

Ukraine claims US missile holdup ahead of reported talks

TRUMP PRESSURE Despite the apparently cordial nature of Tuesday's meeting in Oslo, Trump, as he showed in comments in the White House on Tuesday, remains frustrated with Zelenskyy, whom he has repeatedly rebuked and suggested needs to be replaced.
"He's going to have to want to make a deal, because I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer," Trump told reporters on the eve of the talks in Russia.
Putin, who has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine and no NATO membership for Kyiv, will receive Witkoff in the Constantine Palace, a grand imperial edifice in what is the Kremlin chief's home city.
Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy and his main point man for potential economic and financial deals with the US, would also be present at the meeting with Witkoff, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said.
A US official said Ukraine had brought new ideas and proposals to the Oslo talks, which had made "meaningful progress" toward a coordinated approach to engaging with Russia.
The official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the talks covered "key elements of a comprehensive peace framework", including security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war economic plan and a broader European security architecture.
Witkoff would aim to "create a pathway toward direct trilateral and broader multilateral negotiations," the official said. Zelenskyysaid he hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump.
The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskyy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile and that a lot of the legwork required for an overall agreement would need to be in place.
Trump said on Tuesday he had raised the idea with Putin of freeing Stephen Hubbard - a 74-year-old retired US school teacher being held in Russia on mercenary charges he denies.
Putin told Witkoff that Hubbard was at the airport waiting to fly back to the United States with him. Witkoff thanked Putin for the goodwill gesture.
Hubbard was first detained in April 2022 and was later sentenced to six years and 10 months on charges whose veracity his family and US-based lawyer question.

Source: Reuters/nh

Here are details of Hubbard's case:
WHO IS STEPHEN HUBBARD? Hubbard, 74, a retired schoolteacher, grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by the New York Times.
He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izyum in eastern Ukraine with a Ukrainian partner, according to his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox.
Fox told Reuters in 2024 that Hubbard subsisted on a pension of about $300 a month and had few connections with local people. The siblings last spoke in September 2021.
HOW WAS HE CAPTURED? Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022 and captured Izyum two months later. Ukrainian forces retook the city in September 2022, but Hubbard was already in Russian custody by then.
Russian state media said Hubbard had been detained in April 2022 and alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture.
Fox said she recognised her brother in a YouTube video showing a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. Another video showed him with his hands bound, being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the videos were recorded.
WHY WAS HE IMPRISONED? Following a closed trial, a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary in October 2024 and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison.Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month. Russian state media said he had pleaded guilty to the charges he faced.
Fox questioned the reported confession, however, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian views and was unlikely to have taken up arms in his seventies.
Martin De Luca, his US-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit. He cited Hubbard as telling him Russian soldiers had simply grabbed him from his house.
WHAT IS HUBBARD'S CURRENT STATUS? In January 2025, Washington designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained, enabling the US government to pursue negotiations for his release.
The State Department has said Russia refused to grant US officials consular access.
The New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been moved through at least five Russian detention centres before his trial.
His lawyer said Hubbard's legal team found out only in April 2025 that he was being held in a facility in the Mordovia region, east of Moscow.

items.body:
[バスラ ２１日 ロイター] - イラクの国境当局者は２１日、イランとの国境にある交通量の多いシーブ検問所を閉鎖し、治安状況の評価や、禁止物品の密輸を阻止するための検査装置の設置を行っていると述べた。

同検問所の他の関係筋２人によると、追って通知があるまで、乗客、車両、商用トラックの通行が禁止される。

イラクは９月、サウジアラビアに対するドローン（無人機）攻撃を受けた予防措置として、イランとのもう一つの国境検問所であるシャラムチェの閉鎖を命令。サウジ当局は、ドローンがイラクから発射されたと主張していた。

 イラクの国境検問所当局者はロイターに対し、シーブ検問所における現在の治安対策は脆弱で不十分だと語った。

items.title: Russia frees retired US schoolteacher in goodwill gesture as Putin meets Witkoff
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired US schoolteacher in custody since 2022, from prison on Wednesday and took him to St Petersburg to fly back to the United States, after talks that Washington said were a step toward ending the war in Ukraine.
items.body:
Russia freed [USN:L8N4670PP TEXT:"Stephen Hubbard"], a retired US schoolteacher in custody since 2022, from prison on Wednesday and took him to St Petersburg to fly back to the United States, after talks that Washington said were a step toward ending the war in Ukraine.
Russian President Vladimir Putin made the announcement at a meeting in St Petersburg with US envoy Steve Witkoff, who later said the talks will continue toward planned technical-level discussions involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
Witkoff called Putin a "humanitarian" in thanking him for the move, a remark that drew sharp rebuke from Republican and Democratic lawmakers given Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The prisoner release comes as President Donald Trump's recent gestures toward Moscow, including a deal to buy Russian diesel and a waiver of new sanctions, have already sparked bipartisan pushback in the US Congress and worry in European capitals.
Putin's spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said Putin had freed Hubbard, 74, at Trump's request, and that he had also taken into account the American's poor health. Trump later confirmed he had asked Putin on a call in recent days, and Putin agreed.
"The president sends his thanks, our whole nation sends their thanks, because of Stephen Hubbard," Witkoff told Putin in the meeting shown on Russian state TV. "Because of you he's going home to his family."
In a video shared with Reuters, Hubbard, wearing a dark fleece and clean-shaven, is seen in an undisclosed location in Russia shaking Witkoff's hand and thanking him. Later, Trump posted a picture of Hubbard appearing inside a plane with others and holding an American flag.
Hubbard's son, Joseph Coleman, told Reuters in a voice message that he spoke briefly by phone with his father before he boarded the airplane in Russia.
"Today he seemed light in his step, a sense of happiness in his voice", Coleman said.
THREE-WAY MEETING PLANNED ON WAR Witkoff called the talks with Putin "constructive" and said in a post on X that he had also met Ukrainian and European leaders in Oslo to advance Trump's mission to end the war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he supported the US proposal for three-way talks with Russia and the United States at the level of negotiators to be held as soon as possible, preferably by early November.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere, who also met Witkoff, had earlier said the talks will likely happen in mid-November and focus on a potential post-conflict security structure.
On Wednesday evening, officials in Kyiv said Russian forces attacked the capital city with ballistic missiles that damaged homes and a petrol station and caused injuries.
'HUMANITARIAN' Witkoff's praise for Putin over Hubbard's release was scorned by some in Washington. "Look up the definition of 'humanitarian.' What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say," Republican US Senator Thom Tillis said in an X post directed at the US envoy.
Trump, asked about Witkoff's "humanitarian" comment, told reporters at the White House: “Well, I guess you have to say for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man, who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life, out. But I wouldn't say anything one way or the other."
The US "gave nothing in exchange" for the prisoner release, Trump said, adding "we're getting closer" to settling the war.
"He is the happiest man around," Trump said of Hubbard. "This was very surprising to him, but I did it, it really took place on a phone call at the end of last week with President Putin, so we appreciate it very much. And his family is extremely happy."
FAMILY, LAWYER DISPUTED CONVICTION Hubbard, a native of Michigan, had been serving a prison sentence of six years and 10 months in Russia following a conviction for mercenary activity in a closed-door trial.
He was arrested in April 2022 in the eastern Ukrainian city of Izyum, where Russian prosecutors alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint.
Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month.
Russian state media reported he pleaded guilty to the charges. But Hubbard's US-based lawyer, Martin De Luca, previously told Reuters that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit.
In a 2024 interview with Reuters, Hubbard's sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, also disputed the idea that her brother took up arms for any government, calling him "so non-military" and pointing out his advanced age.
De Luca on Wednesday thanked Trump, Witkoff and other US officials for securing the release, calling it "a dividend earned along the hard road to peace".
As of Wednesday, Hubbard was the only US prisoner held by Russia who was designated by Washington as "wrongfully detained".
The Trump administration secured the release last year of another American jailed in Russia, schoolteacher [USN:S0N3P202G TEXT:"Marc Fogel"], who had been serving a 14-year prison term for drug smuggling.

items.title: Putin agrees to resume 3-way peace talks with Ukraine and US
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
items.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
The negotiations in a grand imperial palace in St Petersburg, the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of [USN:L8N4670PP TEXT:"Stephen Hubbard, a retired US school teacher"] held in Russia whom US President Trump had asked the Kremlin chief to release.
Wednesday's encounter unfolded amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications.
The latest talks also came more than two years since Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours.
The Kremlin said the new 3-way peace talks, which would be at a technical level, could take place in Abu Dhabi and would be focused on how to guarantee the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war ended. They could begin sometime on or after November 10, it said. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran .
The Kremlin was less upbeat, however, about the outcome of talks Witkoff had held a day earlier in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the leaders of Finland and Norway, and European and NATO representatives. Witkoff told Putin the talks had been characterised by "some degree of momentum" and a US official said Ukraine had brought [USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"new ideas and proposals"].
"These nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the St Petersburg meeting - which lasted nearly three hours.
POSSIBLE MEETING BETWEEN TRUMP, PUTIN AND XI Ukraine and Russia remain far apart when it comes to the terms of any possible peace deal, though Trump has recently intensified pressure on Ukraine to strike some kind of a deal. He said on Tuesday it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing."
Putin also used Wednesday's talks to offer to help Trump deal with Iran, saying Russia had a decades-long relationship with Tehran which it has repeatedly offered to leverage to address US concerns about Iran's nuclear programme. Putin told Witkoff it was possible and necessary to get a deal with Tehran, the Kremlin said.
Russia could also supply vast quantities of fertiliser to the United States to help US farmers, the Russian president told Witkoff.
[USN:L1N4650BJ TEXT:"A potential meeting in China next month"] with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was also discussed. The Kremlin said Beijing was already preparing what it said would be the first meeting of its kind in history.
'NEW IDEAS' Putin has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, no NATO membership for Kyiv, and an overall peace deal rather than a temporary ceasefire.
Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy, was also present at the talks with Witkoff and the Kremlin said that major joint economic projects had been discussed, including some that were close to being realised.
Witkoff said he had brought some documents with him containing various ideas for a potential peace deal for Putin to review, and that Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, also wanted to convey some ideas to Putin. Kushner later joined the meeting remotely by phone.
Zelenskiy said he [USN:L1N4670EW TEXT:"hoped to discuss key issues"] on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump.
The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskiy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile.
FRAYING US-UKRAINE TIES US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections.
Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system, though Zelenskiy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues.
Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated on Wednesday that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink.

[シドニー ２１日 ロイター] - オーストラリアのデ...
items.body:
豪データセンターＮＥＸＴＤＣ、新規開発凍結　時価総額ほぼ半減
10/21 18:15 配信

データセンター運営会社ＮＥＸＴＤＣのロゴ。2026年6月22日、シドニーで撮影。 REUTERS/Hollie Adams

Scott Murdoch　Rajasik Mukherjee

[シドニー ２１日 ロイター] - オーストラリアのデータセンター運営会社ＮＥＸＴＤＣの株価が２１日急落し、時価総額がほぼ半減した。今後１年間の売上高見通しを大幅に引き下げ、開発計画を凍結すると発表したことが響いた。

同社によると、メルボルンの主要プロジェクトの一つで電力網の増強が遅れており、今年度に計上する予定だった売上高約１億４０００万豪ドル（９８００万米ドル）が先送りされる。ＮＥＸＴＤＣは当面、新規開発プロジェクトと用地取得を全て凍結すると説明した。

株価は４１．７％安で取引を終え、時価総額が約３０億豪ドル減少した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）に対する投資家心理はここ数週間で悪化している。急増する計算処理や用地、電力のコストに見合う成果を生むのかを巡り、巨額のＡＩ投資に疑問が広がっている。オーストラリアでは先週、データセンター企業が新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を撤回した。データセンター株やハイテク株が売られ、クレジット投資家はＡＩ関連企業への投資を一段と厳しく選別するようになっている。

ＮＥＸＴＤＣは２０２７年の純売上高を４億７５００万─５億豪ドルと見込む。従来予想の６億１５００万─６億４０００万豪ドルから引き下げた。調整後ＥＢＩＴＤＡ（利払い・税金・償却前利益）予想も、３億８５００万─４億１０００万豪ドルから２億４５００万─２億６５００万豪ドルに引き下げた。いずれも電力網増強の遅れで影響を受ける契約分を除いた数字だ。

同社によると、配電会社ジェメナ・エレクトリシティ・ネットワークスによる工事の遅れで、メルボルンのＭ３データセンターへの次の電力供給拡大は２０２８年になる見通しだ。

ジェメナは地域住民や関係者の反対を受け、Ｍ３への電力供給の増強に必要な電力網工事の一部を中断している。再開は早くても２７年２月になるとみている。

• 年末までに再編を完了する見込み。

items.title: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble
items.author: Raphael Satter, Leo Marchandon, Kanjyik Ghosh, Rajveer Pardesi
items.creator: Raphael Satter, Leo Marchandon, Kanjyik Ghosh, Rajveer Pardesi
items.summary: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.
items.body:
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.
Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes to vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years until they were uncovered using AI, saying all users were "encouraged to update immediately."
With tech firms warning that some hackers were already exploiting the flaws, government agencies across Europe were among those that took sites offline as a precaution.
Because a fix is now public and artificial intelligence tools are able to reverse engineer the bug with little effort, experts said they were bracing for a wave of intrusions as hackers jumped to get ahead of the updates.
AI was powering a "race to exploit," said Costin Raiu, co-founder of cybersecurity research and incident response firm TLP:Black. He said the next step was the "mass compromise of every vulnerable web server on the internet."
PHP — a language that dates back to the early 1990s and initially stood for "Personal Home Page" — underpins huge parts of the public-facing web and is baked into WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento sites, meaning any critical vulnerability potentially has enormous knock-on consequences.
"All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable," said Tiffany Farriss, the interim chief executive of the Drupal Association. "This issue impacts the majority of the internet."
Cybersecurity agencies around the world have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied.
According to data from Censys, the internet intelligence firm, about 1.5 million out of 2.6 million hosts report running a version of PHP for which there is no fix.
The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. The operator of the online encyclopedia Wikipedia also said it had taken down an unspecified number of systems until they could be safely patched, while the Internet Archive, the sprawling online library, said it also briefly went offline to deal with the issue.
Even some world leaders weighed in. The Dutch prime minister said he was closely monitoring the situation. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a post on X said website owners should "check whether your live site uses PHP and prepare to apply the new fix."
BUG FOUND WITH AI The flaw in PHP was discovered using artificial intelligence, two cybersecurity companies said in independent reports. Calif said in a blog post it found the flaws with the help of a large language model on August 1 and had been working on a fix ever since. Alphabet-owned (GOOGL.O) cybersecurity company Wiz said in a blog post that it too had discovered it with the help of Wiz Atlas, its autonomous AI vulnerability research tool, as well as Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.
The vulnerabilities remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade and would have been extraordinarily complicated for a human hacker to take advantage of, Wiz's post said.
"Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale," it said. "With AI, this is no longer a barrier." Calif and Wiz said they coordinated with one another and the PHP team and OpenAI on the discovery.
In a statement, the White House said it was made aware of the flaw on Friday.
In a blog post late on Wednesday, Amazon (AMZN.O) security chief CJ Moses said the tech giant's security team detected an attempt to exploit the vulnerabilities against one of its decoy "honeypot" systems on October 17, four days before public disclosure.
The attempt on the system came from an anonymous internet address, suggesting the activity was conducted by a threat actor, Moses said, adding it was unclear how the actor learned of the flaws while they were under embargo.
More attempts followed on Wednesday by multiple actors before the embargo lifted. Amazon said it was still unclear whether any of the attempts would have worked against real websites, adding the flaws were "now being broadly exploited in the wild."
CRITICAL SOFTWARE PHP is a [USN:L6N467127 TEXT:"programming language"] used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP assembles the content and sends it to the browser. It is free, open-source software maintained by volunteers.
Its ubiquity — PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs — has made experts anxious. AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have [USN:L6N46118G TEXT:"proliferated in recent weeks"], could wreak havoc on unpatched servers, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London.
"The scale is huge, and with AI, exploitation may happen instantly," Olejnik said.
WordPress.com operator Automattic said users of its hosted solutions and Tumblr were safe from the bug . Risks were higher for small PHP-powered websites run by individuals or organizations with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly manage the underlying servers.
MASS OUTAGES In the Netherlands, several organizations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites for the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites.
Danish municipal IT company Kombit said it had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform.
Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure."
France's Interior Ministry said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance.
items.raw_description: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.

items.title: 英ＣＰＩ上昇率、9月は前年比3.5％に加速　借入額も予想上回る
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Suban Abdulla

[ロンドン ２１日 ロイター] - 英国立統計局（ＯＮＳ）が２１日発表した９月の消費者物価...
items.body:
英ＣＰＩ上昇率、9月は前年比3.5％に加速　借入額も予想上回る
10/21 16:27 配信

写真は英ロンドンにある食料品店の買い物客。2023年5月撮影。REUTERS/Emilie Madi

Suban Abdulla

[ロンドン ２１日 ロイター] - 英国立統計局（ＯＮＳ）が２１日発表した９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）上昇率は前年同月比３．５％となり、８月の３．１％から加速した。予想（３．４％）を上回り、来週発表の予算案で家計への支援を求める声がさらに高まるほか、１１月の利上げ根拠も強まりそうだ。

ＯＮＳによると、ガソリンとディーゼル（軽油）の価格高騰が原因で、インフレ率は２０２５年１０月以来の高水準に達した。

英中央銀行は７月に発表した見通しで、上昇率は３．０％にとどまると予測していた。

中銀が基調的な物価圧力指標と見なしているサービス部門の物価上昇率は、８月の３．４％から９月は３．７％に拡大。エコノミスト予想の３．６％を上回った。

食料品、エネルギー、アルコール・たばこを除いたコアインフレ率は、２．６％から２．８％に上昇し、これも予想を上回った。

９月のインフレ率は、政府が社会保障給付の増額幅を決定する際に参考にしている指標となる。

PwC UKのエコノミスト、アダム・ディーシー氏は「インフレ率が４％に近づくにつれ、このショックを単に無視することは難しくなっている」と指摘。「インフレ率が高水準で長く続くほど、賃金や価格設定の動向に影響を及ぼし始めるリスクが高まり、そうした『二次的な』影響の明確な証拠を待ち続けることのリスクも増大する」とした。

別の統計によると、政府の借入額は予想を上回り、公的債務残高は３兆ポンドを突破した。ヒーリー財務相が２８日に初めて発表する予算案で直面する課題が浮き彫りになった。

レゾリューション・ファウンデーションの暫定チーフエコノミスト、グレッグ・スウェイツ氏は「インフレの上昇と過去最高水準の債務は、財務相が直面しているジレンマ――政府の借入を抑制しつつ、家計の生活費負担をどのように軽減するか――を如実に示している」と述べた。

キャピタル・エコノミクスの副チーフエコノミスト、ルース・グレゴリー氏は、ここ数カ月の借入額が予想を上回ったことについて、「経済への差し引きの影響が小さく、最も厳しい財政上の選択を来年に先送りする慎重な予算案を２８日に財務相が提示するというわれわれの見方を裏付けるものだ」と語った。

ＯＮＳが別途発表したデータは、今後インフレ圧力が高まる可能性を示唆。９月の工場出荷価格は前年比４．６％上昇し、伸び率は８月の３．８％から加速。２３年４月以来最大の上昇幅となった。

製造業の投入コストは、８月の６．７％上昇に続き８．３％上昇し、市場予想の７．２％上昇を上回った。

items.body:
訪日外国人、9月は5.0％減　中東情勢や台風が打撃
10/21 16:17 配信

写真は10月12日、東京・渋谷の横断歩道で撮影。REUTERS/Kevin Coombs

Shiho Tanaka

[東京 ２１日 ロイター] - 日本政府観光局（ＪＮＴＯ）が２１日発表した９月の訪日外国人客数は、前年同月比５．０％減の３１０万３７００人だった。中東情勢を受けた航空券価格の上昇に加え、航空便の減便や台風による欠航が全体として訪日客数を押し下げた。

一方、国・地域別に見ると、韓国、メキシコ、中東地域など７市場からの客数は９月として過去最高を記録した。愛知県でアジア競技大会が開催され、選手や関係者による訪⽇需要もあった。中国は、日本への渡航自粛の注意喚起や航空便の減便が影響し４４．５％減と、引き続き大幅減となっている。

１月から９月の累計は前年同期比２．９％減の３０７３万０２００人で、昨年に続き９月時点で３０００万人を超えた。

items.title: アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（21日）
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に...
items.body:
アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（21日）
10/21 16:13 配信

中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に向けた大型景気刺激策への期待後退がセンチメントを圧迫した。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１％安で引け、２０２５年８月以来の安値となった。上海総合指数は０．６％安。

香港のハンセン指数は０．９％安。

ハンセンテック指数は、中国が市場下支えのために大規模な景気刺激策を導入した２０２４年９月以来の安値に沈んだ。

中国のバッテリー最大手 のＣＡＴＬ株は香港・本土市場ともに１０％超急落。競争激化と中国の自動車販売の伸び鈍化を受け、第３・四半期の利益成長が大幅に減速したと発表した。

玩具メーカー、ポップマートの業績不振もリスク回避姿勢を強めた。株価は２１日に５％下落。第３・四半期決算が失望視されるとと見込まれる中、今月１５％下げている。

市場関係者によると、投資家は第３・四半期の決算発表を前に、消費関連株の売買を通じて中国国内需要の弱さに対する弱気の見方を示している。経済成長が引き続き堅調な中、政策当局が早期に市場刺激策を打ち出す公算は小さいとみられている。

バークレイズはリポートで、輸出主導の産業が堅調なため引き続き内需の弱さを覆い隠していると指摘。「成長目標がほぼ達成されており、大規模な景気刺激策導入のハードルは高まったとみている」との見方を示した。

酒類と新エネルギー関連企業が下げを主導した一方、医薬品、通信、クラウドコンピューティング関連企業は相場をアウトパフォームした。

ジュリアス・ベアのエコノミスト、ソフィー・アルターマット氏はリポートで「政府の焦点は、短期的な成長押し上げよりも、技術進歩、産業の高度化、自給率の一段の向上に引き続き置かれている」と指摘した。

市場関係者によると、短期的にはより厳格な税制政策も株式相場の重しとなっている。

ロイターの報道によると、中国政府は富裕層に対し、海外信託関連の所得税を１０月２２日までに申告・納税するよう求めた。これを受け、現金確保のため株式を売却する動きが一部で広がっている。

小型株中心の深セン総合指数は０．４９％安、新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は１．６２％下落、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は０．０６％高。

ソウル株式市場は３％超急反発し、約６週間ぶりの大幅高となった。好調な輸出や業績見通しの上方修正を受け人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株などを巡る投資家心理が改善した。

総合株価指数（ＫＯＳＰＩ）は３．２９％高で終了、９月７日以来の大幅な上昇率となった。

税関当局のデータによると、今月１─２０日の輸出は前年同期比で倍以上に増加した。世界的なＡＩ投資を背景に半導体販売が記録的水準となった。

サーバー製造の米スーパー・マイクロ・コンピューターは２０日の時間外取引で急伸した。ＡＩデータセンター需要の底堅さを背景に、四半期の売上高と利益率がアナリスト予想を大幅に上回るとの見通しを示した。この強気見通しがＡＩ関連株を押し上げた。

半導体大手サムスン電子は５．６７％高、同業のＳＫハイニックスは５．８１％高。

ＡＩインフラ企業エリス・グループは３０％急伸し、２０日の市場デビューでの急落から反発した。

取引された９１５銘柄のうち、３７１銘柄が上昇、４９１銘柄が下落した。

海外投資家は６６００億ウォン（４億９８３８万ドル）相当の買い越しとなった。

シドニー株式市場は上下に振れた取引のなか小幅上昇して引けた。銀行株の上昇が鉱業株とデータセンター運営のＮＥＸＴＤＣの下落を相殺した。投資家は中央銀行高官からのインフレに関する厳しい警告を消化した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ／ＡＳＸ２００指数は０．２％高で終了。一時０．２％下げた。

ＮＥＸＴＤＣは取引時間中に４５％超急落、約９年ぶりの大幅安となり時価総額のほぼ半分を失った。同社は来年度の売上高予想を下方修正し、今後の開発を一時停止すると発表した。これを受けてＩＴ株指数は一時６．１％下落し、４月中旬以来の大幅安を記録した。

バンテージ・マーケッツの市場アナリスト、ヒービー・チェン氏は、今回の急落は人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームの不都合な現実を浮き彫りにしたと指摘。「インフラのボトルネックにより需要が売り上げに結び付かなければ、強い需要も目先の業績にはほとんど意味がない」と述べた。

鉱業株指数は１．２％下落。四半期の銅生産量が予想を下回ったＢＨＰは軟調。

銀行株指数は１％上昇、四大銀行株は全て上昇した。メリウェザー・キャピタルのポートフォリオマネジャー、ルーク・ウィンチェスター氏は「銀行株が上昇した最大の理由は、ＮＥＸＴＤＣが引き起こした不透明感を受けて、資金を退避させる逃避先として位置付けられた」と述べた。

オーストラリア準備銀行（中央銀行）のハウザー副総裁が、金融引き締めは効果を上げているものの、インフレは「著しく悪化した」ように見え、原油高が大きな要因となっていると発言、センチメントに影響した。

インフレ見通しへの懸念から、市場では１１月の利上げ確率が週初めの３０％から４４％超に上昇。１２月の利上げ確率も６４％に上昇した。

エネルギー株指数は０．５％高。サントスが０．５％高、ウッドサイドは年間生産見通しの上限を引き下げたものの、０．４％上昇した。

items.author: ロイター

items.summary: [東京 ２１日 ロイター] - 東京株式市場で日経平均は反発し、前営業日比０．８５％（５４５円８２銭）高の６万４６２１円...
items.body:
日経平均は反発、ＡＩ・半導体株中心に幅広く物色
10/21 16:11 配信

写真は4月6日、東京証券取引所で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

[東京 ２１日 ロイター] - 東京株式市場で日経平均は反発し、前営業日比０．８５％（５４５円８２銭）高の６万４６２１円２４銭で取引を終えた。これまでの下落に対して突っ込み警戒感も生じており、人工知能（ＡＩ）・半導体関連株を中心に幅広く買いを誘う格好となった。ただ、上値を追うだけの材料に乏しく、中盤からは伸び悩んだ。

引き続き、原油価格の高止まりなどから、インフレ懸念が残っているものの、米国においてハイテク企業の好決算が目立ったことが、買い材料として注目された。

中でも、米国で注目されていたスペースＸの決算が上場後四半期で初めて黒字化するなど予想以上に好調だったことがＡＩ・半導体関連株に買い安心感を誘ったほか、韓国ＫＯＳＰＩの上昇もプラス材料となった。

ただ、「目先的には材料となるイベントが見当たらず、国内では上半期の決算発表待ち。それを見極めたいとのムードもあり、全体的に上値追いとならない」（国内証券ストラテジスト）との指摘もあり、中盤からは伸び悩む展開となった。

市場では「地合いは回復したものの、このまま調整が深かったＡＩ株を買っていいのか、バリュー株を狙うのか物色面で迷いが生じているようだ。決算発表の数値を見てからとの雰囲気もあり、物色の柱が定まるのはそれからになりそうだ」（岡地証券・投資情報室長の森裕恭氏）との声が聞かれた。

ＴＯＰＩＸは０．８６％高の４０４３．７３ポイントで取引を終えた。東証プライム市場指数は前営業日比０．８６％高の２０８３．９６ポイントだった。プライム市場の売買代金は６兆９２６５億６９００万円だった。

東証３３業種では、値上がりは非鉄金属、銀行業、保険業など２４業種、値下がりは小売業、パルプ・紙など９業種。

個別では、アドバンテスト、イビデン、ソフトバンクグループなどが堅調となったほか、あいちフィナンシャルグループなど地銀株の一角も高いが、トヨタ自動車はさえない。

新興株式市場は、東証グロース市場２５０指数が上昇し、２．７９％（２０．７８ポイント）高の７６６．６９ポイントだった。

東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが９８２銘柄（６３％）、値下がりは５２１銘柄（３３％）、変わらずは５０銘柄（３％）だった。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Vibhuti Sharma　Aditya Kalra

[ムンバイ ２１日 ロイター] - 印リライアンス傘下のジオ・...
items.body:
印ジオＩＰＯ、2時間足らずで応募が募集株数に到達
10/21 16:09 配信

写真は印リライアンス傘下のジオ・プラットフォームズのロゴと人影。3月24日、ムンバイで撮影。REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

Vibhuti Sharma　Aditya Kalra

[ムンバイ ２１日 ロイター] - 印リライアンス傘下のジオ・プラットフォームズによる３２億ドル規模の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）は２１日、一般向けの申し込み開始から２時間足らずで応募が募集株数に達した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）関連企業を選別する投資家の目が厳しくなる中、今回のＩＰＯは、世界の投資家の新規公開株への投資意欲を測る重要な試金石となる。

ジオ・プラットフォームズは、メタやアルファベット傘下のグーグル、機関投資家の出資を受けている。契約者数５億人超のインド最大の通信会社を傘下に持ち、単一国内の契約者数では中国移動に次ぐ世界２位の通信事業者となっている。

取引所が２１日公表したデータによると、機関投資家の応募は割当枠の３．２５倍に達した。募集株数の約３分の１が割り当てられた個人投資家の応募は、これまでのところ割当枠の０．２２倍となっている。

ＩＰＯに基づくジオ・プラットフォームズの評価額は最大１０８３億ドルで、２８日に取引が始まれば、時価総額でインド有数の企業となる可能性がある。

個人投資家、従業員、リライアンスの株主がＩＰＯに申し込むことができ、２３日が期限となっている。仮条件は１株当たり１０６５─１１１９ルピーに設定された。

ジオ・プラットフォームズの３月期の売上高は１５５億ドル、利益は約３２億ドルだった。売上高、利益ともに約９０％を通信事業が占めた。

Australia lawmaker wounded in car attack has lost both her legs: Husband

Doctors worked for days to save Helen Haines' right leg but were ultimately unsuccessful, said her husband.

Members of the police stand guard at the crime scene of a vehicle attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in Wangaratta, Australia, Oct 19, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a video. (Image: Australian Broadcasting Corporation/via Reuters)

SYDNEY: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs amputated after being rammed by a car outside her electoral office, her husband said on Wednesday (Oct 21), as the man accused of the attack appeared in court .
Doctors amputated Haines' left leg after the alleged attacker struck her twice with his car in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, on Monday, Phil Haines said. They worked for days to save her right leg but were ultimately unsuccessful, he told a press conference in Melbourne.
"The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she's stable. That is the most important thing for our family," he said.
Brendan Nugent , a 43-year-old resident of the rural town of Tarrawingee within Haines' electorate, was charged with three offences: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a public official.
